concepts.name: Occasionalism
concepts.definition: Doctrine that God is the sole real cause and creates all events at every moment.

books.evidence: God as sole real cause, denying causal efficacy to natural processes.

books.evidence: Critiques Ash'arite denial of real causal powers in nature.

books.title: Nihaya al-iqdam
books.evidence: Defends doctrine that God alone causes all events, no real causal efficacy in creation.

figures.name: Al-Baydawi

figures.name: Ibn Arabi

figures.evidence: Ibn al-Jawzi transmitted jurisprudential knowledge foundational to maqasid discourse without direct systematic treatment.

figures.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
figures.evidence: Ibn Qudama addressed purposes in Hanbali law but did not systematically develop maqasid framework.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Banna's scientific work has minimal direct connection to maqasid al-shari'a objectives.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Qayyim explicitly developed maqasid theory as central to Islamic jurisprudential methodology.

figures.name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
figures.evidence: Ibn Rajab transmitted maqasid concepts in Hanbali jurisprudence without foundational theoretical innovation.

figures.name: Shah Waliullah
figures.evidence: Shah Waliullah systematically reformulated maqasid al-shari'a as core Islamic legal philosophy.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Ibn Taymiyya's jurisprudence prioritized protection of religion, life, intellect, and property objectives.

figures.name: Abd al-Aziz Ibn Baz
figures.evidence: Ibn Baz transmitted orthodox jurisprudence referencing maqasid without developing original theoretical framework.

concepts.definition_ar: قراءة الشريعة من خلال غاياتها العليا كحفظ النفس والدين والعقل
concepts.definition_ur: شریعت کو اس کے اعلیٰ مقاصد جیسے حفظِ نفس، دین اور عقل سے سمجھنا

concepts.name: Daruriyyat, hajiyyat, tahsiniyyat
concepts.definition: Tripartite ranking of legal interests as necessities, needs, and refinements.
concepts.definition_ar: تصنيف ثلاثي للمصالح الشرعية إلى ضروريات وحاجيات وتحسينيات.
concepts.definition_ur: شرعی مصالح کی تین سطحوں میں تقسیم: ضروریات، حاجیات، اور تحسینیات۔

concepts.name: Sadd al-dhara'i' (blocking the means)
concepts.definition: Prohibiting otherwise lawful acts that predictably lead to forbidden outcomes.
concepts.definition_ar: منع أفعال مباحة في الأصل لأنها تؤدي إلى محرّمات
concepts.definition_ur: جائز افعال کی ممانعت جب وہ حرام نتائج کا ذریعہ بنیں

concepts.name: Fath al-dhara'i' (opening the means)
concepts.definition: Permitting acts that lead to recognized goods even if otherwise restricted.
concepts.definition_ar: إباحة الأعمال التي تؤدي إلى مقاصد معروفة وإن كانت مقيدة في الأصل.
concepts.definition_ur: ان اعمال کو جائز قرار دینا جو معروف نیک مقاصد کی طرف لے جاتے ہوں خواہ اصل میں محدود ہوں۔

concepts.name: 'Urf (custom)

books.evidence: Treats custom as qualifier for rulings across worship and transactions.

books.title: Inscriptions on the Upasaka Sutra

books.title: Dictionnaire Amoureux de l'Algérie

books.title: Eqtedhaa Alseratt Almustaqeem

figures.name: Imam Abu Hanifa

figures.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
figures.evidence: Al-Muwatta gives weight to the customary practice ('amal) of the people of Medina.

figures.name: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd
figures.evidence: Applied Egyptian custom in legal reasoning, differing from Medinan practice.

figures.name: Abu Yusuf
figures.evidence: Incorporated local custom in practical rulings as Chief Qadi across diverse regions.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Shaybani
figures.evidence: Applied custom in legal reasoning following Hanafi school's pragmatic approach.

figures.name: Sahnun
figures.evidence: Applied Maliki custom principles to North African context as Qadi of Kairouan.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Mabsut discusses custom's role in applying Hanafi legal principles to practical cases.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah analyzes custom as foundation of social cohesion and legal variation.

figures.name: Al-Wansharisi
figures.evidence: Al-Mi'yar documents and applies Maghribi commercial and agricultural customs in Maliki rulings.

figures.name: Ebussuud Efendi
figures.evidence: Integrated Ottoman customary law (kanun) with Hanafi fiqh in legal opinions.

figures.name: Ashraf Ali Thanvi
figures.evidence: Applied custom-sensitive rulings to Indian Muslim contexts in Behishti Zewar.

figures.name: Qasim Amin
figures.evidence: Challenged Egyptian customs confining women as un-Islamic cultural accretions, not authentic law.

figures.name: Tahir ibn Ashur
figures.evidence: Emphasized custom's role in legal adaptation within maqasid-based methodology.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: Engaged custom as source for adapting rulings to varied Muslim-minority contexts in fatwas.

figures.name: Zheng He
figures.evidence: Zheng He's voyages documented diplomatic customs; no direct legal-theological writings on urf preservation survive.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya

figures.name: Malek Chebel
figures.evidence: Chebel's philosophy engaged Islamic tradition including custom's role; moderate treatment of urf in legal thought.

concepts.definition_ar: العادة المحلية بوصفها مصدراً ثانوياً يشكّل تطبيق الأحكام
concepts.definition_ur: مقامی رواج بطور ثانوی ماخذ جو احکام کے اطلاق کو متعین کرے

concepts.name: Istishab (presumption of continuity)
concepts.definition: Presuming a prior legal state to continue absent evidence of change.
concepts.definition_ar: افتراض استمرار الحالة المعلومة حتى يثبت تغيّرها
concepts.definition_ur: معلوم حالت کے جاری رہنے کا فرض جب تک تبدیلی ثابت نہ ہو

concepts.name: Bara'a asliyya (original non-liability)
concepts.definition: Default principle that persons are free of obligation until proven otherwise.
concepts.definition_ar: المبدأ الأصلي أن الشخص معفو عن التكليف حتى يثبت خلاف ذلك.
concepts.definition_ur: بنیادی اصول کہ شخص ذمہ داری سے آزاد ہے جب تک ثبوت نہ ہو۔

concepts.name: Ibaha asliyya (presumption of permissibility)
concepts.definition: Default that things are permissible unless a text prohibits them.

books.title: The Lawful and the Prohibited in Islam
books.evidence: Central thesis: things are lawful unless text forbids them.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: al-Qaradawi explicitly formulated ibaha asliyya as foundational principle in Islamic jurisprudence and methodology.

concepts.definition_ar: الأصل أن الأشياء مباحة حتى يثبت من النص ما يحرمها.
concepts.definition_ur: اصول یہ ہے کہ چیزیں جائز ہیں جب تک نص سے تحریم ثابت نہ ہو۔

concepts.name: Amm and khass (general and particular)
concepts.definition: How general scriptural expressions interact with particular qualifying texts.

books.title: Al-Risala (Treatise on Islamic Jurisprudence)
books.evidence: The treatise analyzes how general and particular textual expressions interact.

books.title: Sharh Mushkil al-Athar
books.evidence: Resolving problematic hadiths requires general-particular text harmonization.

books.title: Aḥkām al-Qurʼān al-Karīm
books.evidence: Deriving legal rulings requires analyzing general and particular Quranic expressions.

books.title: ِAl-Nāsikh Wa-Al-Mansūkh

books.title: al-Najm al-wahhāj fī sharḥ al-Minhāj
books.evidence: General-particular textual analysis foundational to this commentary genre.

books.title: Ma'ruzat
books.evidence: General/particular expressions central to legal hermeneutics.

books.title: Al-Fauzul Kabeer Fee Usulit Tafseer

figures.name: Al-Tahawi

figures.name: Ibn Hazm

figures.name: Al-Damiri

figures.name: Ebussuud Efendi

figures.name: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id

concepts.definition_ar: دراسة تفاعل العبارات الشرعية العامة مع النصوص المقيدة الخاصة.

concepts.definition: Distinguishing texts requiring clarification from those that clarify them.

books.title: Kitāb Ṣifat al-ṣalāh min sharḥ al-ʻUmdah lil-Imām Muwaffaq al-Dīn Ibn Qudāmah (Dār al-ʻĀṣimah-al-Riyāḍ, H)
books.title_ar: كتاب صفة الصلاة من شرح العمدة للإمام موفق الدين ابن قدامة (دار العاصمة - الرياض، 1429هـ)
books.evidence: Sharḥ focuses on prayer description; fard-wajib distinction present but instrumental.

books.title: Sharḥ ʻUmdat al-fiqh (Dār ʻaṭāʼāt al-ʻIlm, 1440h)
books.evidence: Sharḥ ʻUmdat discusses obligations systematically; fard-wajib distinction substantive but not primary.

figures.name: Al-Tahawi
figures.evidence: Al-Tahawi foundational Hanafi jurist whose works systematized fard-wajib distinctions in obligation theory.

figures.name: Imam Birgivi
figures.evidence: Birgivi transmitted Hanafi-Ottoman legal thought but primarily focused on theological rather than jurisprudential foundations.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Sarakhsi's Mabsut comprehensively elaborated Hanafi fard-wajib framework distinguishing certain from probable evidence grounds.

figures.name: Al-Suyuti
figures.evidence: Al-Suyuti synthesized Islamic jurisprudence broadly but addressed fard-wajib as secondary comparative analysis rather than core doctrine.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.evidence: Al-Ghazali engaged fard-wajib conceptually but emphasized usul theory and theological dimensions over strict Hanafi jurisprudential application.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Qayyim critiqued traditional Hanafi distinctions, offering reformed interpretations rather than straightforward transmission of fard-wajib doctrine.

figures.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
figures.evidence: Ibn Qudama, Hanbali jurist, referenced fard-wajib but operated within different school framework than Hanafi-specific obligation theory.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Ibn Taymiyya rejected conventional fard-wajib distinctions as methodologically flawed, contesting rather than transmitting Hanafi categories.

concepts.definition_ar: تمييز الحنفي بين الواجب المستند لدليل قطعي والواجب المستند لدليل ظني.
concepts.definition_ur: حنفی تمییز: فرض قطعی دلیل سے اور واجب ظنی دلیل سے ثابت۔

concepts.name: Fard kifaya (collective obligation)
concepts.definition: Duties whose performance by some Muslims relieves the obligation from the rest.
concepts.definition_ar: واجبات يسقط أداؤها عن الباقين إذا قام بها البعض من المسلمين.
concepts.definition_ur: وہ واجبات جن کی انجام دہی کچھ مسلمانوں کے ذریعے باقی لوگوں سے ساقط ہو جاتی ہے۔

concepts.name: Rukhsa and 'azima (concession and resolve)
concepts.definition: Distinction between strict legal rulings and concessions granted under hardship.

books.title: Zad al-Ma'ad
books.evidence: Discusses concessions in worship and law based on prophetic practice and hardship.
books.title_ar: زاد المعاد في هدي خير العباد

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Qayyim extensively discussed rukhsa and 'azima in his works on Islamic jurisprudence and legal principles.

concepts.definition_ar: التمييز بين الأحكام الشرعية الصارمة والرخص الممنوحة عند المشقة.
concepts.definition_ur: سخت قانونی احکام اور مشقت کے حالات میں دیے جانے والی رعایتوں میں فرق۔

concepts.name: Darura (necessity)
concepts.definition: The principle that necessity makes the otherwise forbidden permissible within limits.

books.title: The Lawful and the Prohibited in Islam
books.evidence: Develops necessity doctrine extensively for modern hardship cases.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: Al-Qaradawi discussed darura in Islamic jurisprudence but as secondary interpreter rather than originating theorist.

concepts.definition_ar: المبدأ الذي يبيح المحرمات عند الضرورة في حدود معينة.
concepts.definition_ur: وہ اصول جو ضرورت کی صورت میں حرام چیزوں کو حدود کے اندر جائز بناتا ہے۔

concepts.name: Mashaqqa tajlib al-taysir (hardship brings ease)
concepts.definition: Maxim that legal hardship triggers concessions and lighter rulings.
concepts.definition_ar: القاعدة الفقهية بأن المشقة الشرعية توجب الرخصة والتيسير.
concepts.definition_ur: شرعی مشقت رعایتیں اور آسانیاں لازم کرتی ہے۔

concepts.name: Qawa'id fiqhiyya (legal maxims)
concepts.definition: Concise principles synthesizing rulings across diverse cases.

books.title: I'lam bi-hudud qawa'id al-islam
books.evidence: Title 'qawa'id al-islam' directly indicates legal maxims and foundational principles

books.title: Jami' al-Mabadi' wa'l-Ghayat
books.evidence: Ibn al-Banna known for synthetic works; 'Principles' suggests systematic legal maxims.

books.title: Jâmi’ al-‘Ulûm wa al-Hikam
books.evidence: Commentary on forty hadiths containing legal maxims and principles across diverse cases.

books.title: et-Tarikatü'l-Muhammediye
books.evidence: Reformist text organizing worship and conduct using general legal principles.

books.title: al-mabsūt (Maṭbaʻat al-Saʻādah, 1906)
books.evidence: Work synthesizes broad legal maxims across diverse cases throughout Mabsut.

books.title: Iḥkām al-Iḥkām sharḥ ʻUmdat al-aḥkām (ʻĀlam al-Kutub, 1407h)
books.evidence: Commentary deriving rulings from hadith likely formulates or applies legal maxims.

books.title: al-Jāmiʻ al-Ṣaghīr wa-maʻahu al-nāfiʻ al-kabīr (1411h)
books.evidence: Text synthesizes legal principles across cases characteristic of Hanafi systematic method.

books.title: Tadhkirat al-Fuqahā
books.evidence: Comprehensive fiqh work synthesizing legal principles across diverse rulings.

books.title: Jāmiʻ al-ʻUlūm wa-al-Ḥikam fī sharḥ khamsīn ḥadīthan min Jawāmiʻ al-Kalim (Muʼassasat al-Risālah, 1417h)
books.evidence: Synthesizes legal maxims across diverse cases in systematic hadith commentary format.
books.title_ar: جامع العلوم والحكم في شرح خمسين حديثاً من جوامع الكلم
books.title_ur: جامع العلوم والحکم فی شرح خمسین حدیثاً من جوامع الکلم

books.title: al-Qawāʻid al-nūrānīyah al-fiqhīyah (Dār Ibn al-Jawzī, 1422h)
books.evidence: Ibn Taymiyya's al-Qawāʻid al-nūrānīyah directly systematizes foundational legal maxims organizing jurisprudential rulings across cases.

figures.name: Al-Qadi Iyad
figures.evidence: Al-Qadi Iyad transmitted jurisprudential knowledge but primarily known as hadith scholar and judge, not maxim systematizer.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi focused on mathematics and astronomy; no direct connection to qawa'id fiqhiyya documented.

figures.name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
figures.evidence: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali authored Qawa'id al-Fiqh, foundational legal maxims text synthesizing Hanbali rulings systematically.

figures.name: Imam Birgivi
figures.evidence: Imam Birgivi engaged jurisprudential principles in theology but not primary contributor to qawa'id fiqhiyya formalization.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Sarakhsi's Usul and jurisprudential works establish foundational legal reasoning principles underlying qawa'id fiqhiyya.

figures.name: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id
figures.evidence: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id wrote on hadith and jurisprudence methodology but not specialist in legal maxims compilation.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Shaybani
figures.evidence: Muhammad al-Shaybani's extensive jurisprudential works establish principles systematized later into formal qawa'id fiqhiyya framework.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Allama Hilli's theological focus and Shi'a orientation distance him from mainstream qawa'id fiqhiyya development.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Ibn Taymiyya addressed jurisprudential principles and usul but reformist approach differs from systematic qawa'id tradition.

concepts.definition_ar: مبادئ موجزة تجمع الأحكام عبر الحالات المختلفة.
concepts.definition_ur: مختصر اصول جو مختلف حالات میں احکام کو جمع کرتے ہیں۔

concepts.name: Furuq (legal distinctions)
concepts.definition: Genre identifying subtle differences between superficially similar legal cases.
concepts.definition_ar: نوع من التأليف يحدد الفروقات الدقيقة بين القضايا الفقهية المتشابهة.
concepts.definition_ur: ایک صنف جو سطحی طور پر ملتے جلتے فقہی مسائل میں لطیف فرق متعین کرتی ہے۔

concepts.name: Ikhtilaf (juristic disagreement)
concepts.definition: The discipline of cataloging and analyzing legitimate differences between jurists.

books.title: Ikhtilaf Abi Hanifa wa Ibn Abi Layla
books.evidence: Title explicitly marks this as a work cataloging legal differences between two jurists.
books.title_ar: اختلاف أبي حنيفة وابن أبي ليلى
books.title_ur: اختلاف ابی حنیفہ وابن ابی لیلیٰ

books.title: Kitaab-ul-Aathaar
books.evidence: Records variant companion and early jurist opinions on cases.

books.title: Al-Mudawana al-Qubra
books.evidence: Mudawana systematically records divergent opinions within Maliki school and beyond.

books.title: Jami al-Tirmidhi (Al-Sunan)
books.evidence: Extensive documentation of juristic differences across Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i schools per hadith.

books.title: Bidayat al-Mujtahid
books.evidence: Core methodology cataloging and analyzing legitimate differences between madhahib.

books.title: Bulūgh al-marām min adillat al-aḥkām
books.evidence: Notes divergent juristic positions derived from different hadiths on issues.

books.title: al-Inṣāf fī bayān asbāb al-Ikhtilāf
books.evidence: Title directly states the work explains causes of juristic differences.

books.title: al-mabsūt (Maṭbaʻat al-Saʻādah, 1906)
books.evidence: Systematically analyzes differences between schools and jurists on each issue.

books.title: Tartīb al-madārik wa-taqrīb al-masālik (Maṭbaʻat Faḍālah, 1965)
books.evidence: Biographical dictionary cataloging Maliki jurists and their legal disputes.

books.title: Kashf al-ẓunūn ʻan asāmī al-Kutub wa-al-Funūn (Muʼassasat al-Furqān lil-Turāth al-Islāmī, 1443h)
books.evidence: Legal theory coverage inherently catalogs literature on juristic disagreement and methodology.
books.title_ar: كشف الظنون عن أسامي الكتب والفنون
books.title_ur: کشف الظنون عن اسامی الکتب والفنون

books.title: al-Wasit fi al-madhhab
books.evidence: Al-Ghazali's al-Wasit systematically presents Shafi'i school jurisprudence with attention to variant positions within the madhhab.

books.title: Mīzān al-muʻaddalah fī shaʼn al-Basmalah (al-Bashāʼir al-Islāmīyah, 2010)
books.title_ar: ميزان المعدلة في شأن البسملة (البشائر الإسلامية، 2010)
books.evidence: Mīzān al-muʻaddalah focuses on Quranic hermeneutics regarding the Basmala, not juristic disagreement cataloging.

books.title: al-Ḥāwī llftāwy (dār al-ktb al-ʿlmīẗʻ, 2000)
books.evidence: Al-Ḥāwī compiles fatwas across issues; includes comparative positions but not systematic ikhtilaf analysis.

books.title: tʿǧīl al-mnfʿẗ bzwāʾid rǧāl al-ʾaʾimẗ al-ʾarbʿẗ (Dār al-Bashāʼir al-Islāmīyah)
books.title_ar: تعجيل المنفعة بزوائد رجال الأئمة الأربعة (دار البشائر الإسلامية)
books.title_ur: تعجيل المنفعة بزوائد رجال الأئمة الأربعة (دار البشائر الإسلامية)
books.evidence: Taʿjīl al-mnfʿẗ is a biographical dictionary of hadith transmitters from four schools, not ikhtilaf study.

books.title: taʿjīl al-manfaʿaẗ bizawāʾid rijāl al-ʾaʾimaẗ al-ʾarbaʿaẗ
books.title_ar: تعجيل المنفعة بزوائد رجال الأئمة الأربعة
books.title_ur: تعجیل المنفعۃ بزوائد رجال الائمۃ الاربعۃ
books.evidence: Same work as item 3; biographical reference on four madhab transmitters, tangential to juristic disagreement.

books.title: al-Mughnī li-Ibn Qudāmah (Maktabat al-Qāhirah, 1389h)
books.evidence: Al-Mughnī systematically analyzes Hanbali positions against other three schools across fiqh topics throughout.

books.title: al-Mughnī (Dār ʻĀlam al-Kutub, 1997)
books.evidence: Al-Mughnī presents detailed Hanbali jurisprudence with extensive comparisons to Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanafi schools.

books.title: Bidāyat al-mujtahid wa-nihāyat al-muqtaṣid (Dār al-ḥadīth, 2004)
books.evidence: Bidāyat al-mujtahid explicitly catalogs juristic disagreements between four schools across Islamic law comprehensively.

books.title: Rafʻ al-malām ʻan al-aʼimmah al-Aʻlām (al-Riʼāsah al-ʻĀmmah lil-Buḥūth al-ʻIlmīyah wa-al-Iftāʼ, 1403h)
books.title_ar: رفع الملام عن الأئمة الأعلام (الرئاسة العامة للبحوث العلمية والإفتاء، 1403هـ)
books.title_ur: رفع الملام عن الأئمة الأعلام (الرئاسة العامة للبحوث العلمية والإفتاء، 1403هـ)
books.evidence: Rafʻ al-malām defends positions of four imams; focuses on vindication rather than neutral ikhtilaf cataloging.

books.title: al-Radd ʻalá al-Subkī fī masʼalat taʻlīq al-ṭalāq (Dār ʻaṭāʼāt al-ʻIlm, 1440h)
books.title_ar: الرد على السبكي في مسألة تعليق الطلاق (دار عطاءات العلم، 1440هـ)
books.title_ur: الرد على السبكي في مسألة تعليق الطلاق
books.evidence: Al-Radd ʻalá al-Subkī addresses specific taʻlīq al-ṭalāq disagreement; polemic against one jurist, not systematic analysis.

figures.name: Shurayh al-Qadi
figures.evidence: Witnessed and navigated differences between companions' rulings across sixty years.

figures.name: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
figures.evidence: Transmitted diverse views from companions like Ibn Abbas on juristic questions.

figures.name: Kharija ibn Zayd ibn Thabit
figures.evidence: Contributed to legitimate diversity of rulings as one of competing Medinan authorities.

figures.name: Makhul al-Shami
figures.evidence: As chief jurist navigated early legal diversity among Syrian scholars and schools.

figures.name: Al-Awza'i
figures.evidence: His Syrian school represented early regional diversity before madhab consolidation.

figures.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
figures.evidence: Al-Muwatta records variant opinions among early Medina jurists on disputed questions.

figures.name: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd
figures.evidence: Preserved legitimate diversity through his independent school rivaling Malik's in Egypt.

figures.name: Abu Yusuf
figures.evidence: Ikhtilaf Abi Hanifa wa Ibn Abi Layla documents juristic disagreements between scholars.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Shaybani
figures.evidence: Recorded Abu Hanifa's disagreements with others in Kitaab-ul-Aathaar systematically.

figures.name: Hisham I of Córdoba
figures.evidence: Suppressed non-Maliki legal schools and burned books of other madhahib in Córdoba.

figures.name: Imam al-Shafi'i
figures.evidence: Kitab Ikhtilaf al-Hadith in al-Umm reconciles contradictory prophetic reports.

figures.name: Sahnun
figures.evidence: Al-Mudawwana systematically records variant opinions within Maliki school.

figures.name: Al-Muzani
figures.evidence: Preserved Shafi'i's positions on juristic disagreement in his legal compendium.

figures.name: Al-Mutawakkil
figures.evidence: Allowed traditional schools to flourish again after ending enforced Mu'tazili uniformity.

figures.name: Al-Tabari
figures.evidence: Documented multiple juristic opinions in his works, preserving early legal disagreement.

figures.name: Ibn Surayj
figures.evidence: Transmitted and systematized positions of juristic disagreement within the Shafi'i school.

figures.name: Sahl al-Su'luki
figures.evidence: Navigated juristic disagreement as mufti addressing diverse legal questions.

figures.name: Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini
figures.evidence: Engaged with juristic disagreement as head of Shafi'i school facing other madhahib.

figures.name: Ibn Hazm
figures.evidence: Attacked legal diversity as deviation, wrote polemics against Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanafi schools.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Mabsut preserves and transmits divergent opinions within Hanafi school and among schools.

figures.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
figures.evidence: Al-Mughni systematically documents and adjudicates juristic disagreements across schools.

figures.name: Ibn Khallikan
figures.evidence: Records biographical details of jurists from multiple schools, documenting the diversity of Islamic law.

figures.name: Khidr Bey
figures.evidence: Administered Hanafi law while engaging diversity of legal opinions in Ottoman judicial system.

figures.name: Zenbilli Ali Efendi
figures.evidence: As chief jurist, navigated Hanafi juristic diversity in multi-school Ottoman legal system.

figures.name: Al-Hajj Salim Suwari
figures.evidence: Famously promoted religious tolerance and coexistence with non-Muslim authorities.

figures.name: Ebussuud Efendi
figures.evidence: Navigated intra-Hanafi disagreements while promoting institutional legal uniformity.

figures.name: Abd al-Wahhab al-Sha'rani
figures.evidence: Al-Yawaqit harmonizes differences among the great imams, showing validity of divergent views.

figures.name: Imam Birgivi
figures.evidence: Criticized excessive juristic diversity and laxity while remaining within Hanafi tradition.

figures.name: Ahmad Baba al-Timbukti
figures.evidence: Nayl al-Ibtihaj records biographical diversity of Maliki scholars and their legal differences.

figures.name: Katip Celebi
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Zunun documents juristic disagreements across schools through comprehensive work cataloging.

figures.name: Abdurauf Fitrat
figures.evidence: Acknowledged legitimate diversity while advocating rational reform in legal matters.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: Promoted tolerance of juristic diversity and legitimate disagreement among schools in numerous works.

figures.name: Abdurrahman Wahid
figures.evidence: Promoted legitimate diversity as foundation for pluralism in Muslim societies.

figures.name: Abdolkarim Soroush
figures.evidence: Championed legitimate pluralism in Islamic interpretation against monolithic readings.

figures.name: Ziauddin Sardar
figures.evidence: Acknowledged diversity of scholarly opinion as editor of Critical Muslim journal.

figures.name: Kahina Bahloul
figures.evidence: References historical diversity of legal opinions to legitimize women leading mixed-gender prayer.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Tirmidhi
figures.evidence: Al-Tirmidhi classified hadith grades but did not systematically catalog juristic disagreement.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Ibn Rushd wrote Bidayat al-Mujtahid analyzing legal schools' differences on substantive issues.

figures.name: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
figures.evidence: Ibn Hajar documented variant readings and hadith chains reflecting juristic methodological divergence.

figures.name: Shah Waliullah
figures.evidence: Shah Waliullah synthesized schools but was not primarily a cataloger of juristic disagreement.

figures.name: Al-Qadi Iyad
figures.evidence: Al-Qadi Iyad systematically analyzed juristic differences in Malikite and comparative legal methodology.

figures.name: Al-Suyuti
figures.evidence: Al-Suyuti's al-Ashbah wa-l-Nazair explicitly catalogs and analyzes juristic disagreement across schools.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.evidence: Al-Ghazali examined juristic methods and disagreements in legal epistemology and usul works.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Ibn Taymiyya critiqued existing schools' positions but focused on reformist methodology over cataloging.

concepts.definition_ar: تنوع الأحكام المشروع بين العلماء المؤهلين والمذاهب الفقهية
concepts.definition_ur: اہل علماء اور فقہی مذاہب کے درمیان احکام کا جائز تنوع

concepts.name: Takhayyur (selecting across schools)
concepts.definition: Modern method of choosing rulings from different schools to address new needs.
concepts.definition_ar: طريقة حديثة لاختيار الأحكام من مختلف المذاهب لمعالجة القضايا الجديدة.
concepts.definition_ur: نئے مسائل کے حل کے لیے مختلف مذاہب سے احکام منتخب کرنے کا جدید طریقہ۔

concepts.name: Talfiq (combining school rulings)
concepts.definition: Constructing a single act from rulings of more than one school, traditionally restricted.
concepts.definition_ar: بناء عمل واحد من أحكام أكثر من مذهب واحد، محظور تقليديا.
concepts.definition_ur: ایک عمل میں سے زیادہ ایک مذہب کے احکام کو ملانا، روایتی طور پر منع ہے۔

concepts.name: Fatwa (juristic responsum)
concepts.definition: A non-binding scholarly legal opinion issued in response to a question.

books.title: Letter of Suleiman the Magnificent to Ebussuud Efendi, 1566
books.evidence: Letter from sultan to chief jurist Ebussuud requesting legal opinion on governance.
books.title_ar: رسالة سليمان القانوني إلى أبي السعود أفندي، 1566

books.title: et-Tarikatü'l-Muhammediye
books.evidence: Reformist work functions as practical legal guidance on worship and permissibility.

books.title: Ruka’at-i-Alamgiri
books.evidence: Collection contains legal opinions and rulings issued by the ruler-jurist.

books.title: Majmūʻ fatāwá wa-maqālāt mutanawwiʻah
books.evidence: Title explicitly identifies work as collection of legal opinions (fatawa).

books.title: al-Ḥāwī llftāwy (dār al-ktb al-ʿlmīẗʻ, 2000)
books.evidence: Al-Suyuti's al-Ḥāwī al-fatāwā is a compilation of fatwas, directly addressing juristic responsa as its primary subject.

figures.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
figures.evidence: Suleiman issued legal opinions (fetwas) through his chief mufti but did not author fatwas directly himself.

figures.name: Imam Birgivi
figures.evidence: Birgivi was an Islamic scholar who authored fatwas and juristic opinions on Islamic law and theology.

figures.name: Aurangzeb
figures.evidence: Aurangzeb sought fatwas from scholars to justify policies but was not a fatwa issuer himself.

figures.name: Abd al-Aziz Ibn Baz
figures.evidence: Ibn Baz served as Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia and issued numerous fatwas on Islamic jurisprudence.

figures.name: Al-Suyuti
figures.evidence: Al-Suyuti was a prolific Islamic scholar who authored fatwas and juristic responsa on various legal matters.

concepts.definition_ar: رأي قانوني غير ملزم يصدره الفقيه ردا على سؤال.
concepts.definition_ur: غیر لازمی قانونی رائے جو فقیہ سوال کے جواب میں جاری کرتا ہے۔

concepts.name: Qada' (judgeship)
concepts.definition: The institution and ethics of judicial office and adjudication.

books.title: Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyyah (The Laws of Islamic Governance)
books.evidence: Extensive treatment of judicial appointment, ethics, and adjudication procedures.

books.title: Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya w'al-Wilayat al-Diniyya
books.evidence: Extensively covers judicial office, appointment, and adjudication procedures.

books.title: Ruka’at-i-Alamgiri
books.evidence: Work addresses judicial practice and adjudication under Mughal administration.

books.title: Explanation And Analysis Of The Giving Judgment
books.evidence: Title 'Explanation of Giving Judgment' directly indicates judicial adjudication focus.

books.title: Al-Aḥkām Al-Sulṭānīyah (Dar Al-Kotob Al-Ilmiyah)
books.evidence: Systematically treats judicial office, appointment, and adjudication procedures.

books.title: Turukul Hikmiyat
books.evidence: Ibn al-Qayyim's work directly addresses judicial wisdom and ethical principles of qada' practice.

books.title: al-Ṭuruq al-Ḥikmīyah fī al-siyāsah al-sharʻīyah (Dār ʻaṭāʼāt al-ʻIlm, 1440h)
books.title_ar: الطرق الحكمية في السياسة الشرعية (دار عطاءات العلم، 1440هـ)
books.evidence: Al-Ṭuruq al-Ḥikmīyah covers Shariah-based governance and judicial administration (siyāsah sharʻīyah).

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Al-Mawardi wrote foundational treatise on qadi appointment, qualifications, and judicial duties in Islamic governance.

figures.name: Aurangzeb
figures.evidence: Aurangzeb appointed qadis and issued decrees on judicial administration but not primary theorist of qada'.

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-shi'r (poetic theory)
concepts.definition: Theoretical reflection on the nature, purposes, and criticism of poetry.

books.title: A'la qadr 'ahl aleazm
books.evidence: Al-Mutanabbi's poem exemplifies poetic practice but lacks explicit theoretical reflection on poetry's nature or criticism.

books.title: Hadikat al-suada
books.evidence: Fuzuli's garden of poets is a poetic work, not a theoretical treatise on poetic theory or criticism.

books.title: The Divān of Hafez
books.evidence: Hafez's Divan is a poetry collection without systematic poetic theory or critical analysis of verse.

books.title: Sarah
books.evidence: El-Akkad's Sarah is a narrative or dramatic work, not theoretical reflection on poetry.

books.title: Diwan-i-Amir Khusru
books.evidence: Amir Khusrau's Divan is a poetry collection without explicit poetic theory or criticism.

books.title: Alfiyyah al-Hadith
books.evidence: Al-Suyuti's Alfiyyah concerns hadith tradition, not poetic theory or criticism.

books.title: Shaqāʾiq al-utrunj fī raqāʾiq al-ghunj
books.evidence: Al-Suyuti's work on eloquence and rhetoric relates secondarily to poetic analysis and language theory.

books.title: Gabriel's Wing
books.evidence: Gabriel's Wing is a poetic work by Iqbal without documented theoretical content on poetry.

books.title: Persian Psalms
books.evidence: Persian Psalms is a poetic collection, not systematic poetic theory or criticism.

books.title: The Rod of Moses
books.evidence: The Rod of Moses is a poetic work, not theoretical reflection on poetry's nature or criticism.

books.title: The Call of the Marching Bell
books.evidence: The Call of the Marching Bell is a poetic composition without explicit poetic theory.

books.title: Makhzan al-Asrar
books.evidence: Makhzan al-Asrar is a narrative poem, not theoretical analysis of poetic principles.

books.title: Khosrow and Shirin
books.evidence: Khosrow and Shirin is a narrative poem exemplifying poetic practice, not poetic theory.

books.title: Heer Ranjha
books.evidence: Heer Ranjha is a folk narrative poem without explicit poetic theory or criticism.

books.title: The introduction of Shakespeare
books.evidence: El-Akkad's introduction of Shakespeare directly addresses poetic theory and dramatic/poetic criticism.

books.title: The gift of the crowne (A poetic collection)
books.evidence: A poetic collection demonstrates poetry but lacks theoretical reflection on poetic nature or criticism.

books.title: Jameel Buthaina
books.evidence: Jameel Buthaina is a poetic work, not theoretical reflection on poetry itself.

books.title: The poet language
books.evidence: El-Akkad's The poet language directly theorizes about poetic language and its principles.

figures.name: Al-Mutanabbi
figures.evidence: Al-Mutanabbi's poetry and self-commentary established foundational poetic standards and criticism in classical Arabic tradition.

figures.name: Al-Suyuti
figures.evidence: Al-Suyuti wrote on rhetoric and literary criticism but primarily focused on jurisprudence and hadith.

figures.name: Nizami Ganjavi
figures.evidence: Nizami's narrative poems embody and theorize poetic structure, aesthetics, and philosophical purposes of Persian poetry.

figures.name: Hafez
figures.evidence: Hafez's ghazals demonstrate refined poetic theory through practice and influence Persian literary critical tradition.

figures.name: Abbas el-Akkad
figures.evidence: Abbas el-Akkad wrote extensive philosophical and critical works on poetry, aesthetics, and literary theory.

figures.name: Allama Iqbal
figures.evidence: Iqbal addressed poetry's spiritual and philosophical role but primarily as philosopher, not systematic poetic theorist.

figures.name: Amir Khusrau
figures.evidence: Amir Khusrau innovated poetic forms and influenced theory but worked mainly as court poet-practitioner.

figures.name: Waris Shah
figures.evidence: Waris Shah's Sufi poetry exemplifies tradition but lacks explicit theoretical reflection on poetic principles.

figures.name: Fuzuli
figures.evidence: Fuzuli's poetry and prefaces explicitly theorize emotional expression, love poetry, and Persian aesthetic principles.

concepts.definition_ar: التأمل النظري في طبيعة الشعر ومقاصده ونقده.
concepts.definition_ur: شاعری کی فطرت، مقاصد اور نقد پر نظریاتی غور و خوض۔

concepts.name: Takhyil (poetic imagination)
concepts.definition: Aristotelian-inspired theory that poetry moves the soul through imaginative assent.

books.title: Middle Commentary on the Rhetoric
books.evidence: Averroes develops imaginative assent theory in his treatment of rhetorical persuasion.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Ibn Rushd's commentaries on Aristotle directly transmitted Aristotelian poetic theory to Islamic and medieval European thought.

concepts.definition_ar: نظرية مستوحاة من أرسطو تقول إن الشعر يحرك الروح بالموافقة التخييلية.
concepts.definition_ur: ارسطو سے متاثر نظریہ کہ شاعری خیالی قبول سے روح کو متحرک کرتی ہے۔

concepts.name: Sariqat shi'riyya (poetic plagiarism)
concepts.definition: The critical analysis of how later poets borrow motifs and phrases from predecessors.

books.title: al-Ghayth al-musajjam fī sharḥ Lāmīyat al-ʻAjam
books.evidence: Commentary likely traces al-Tughrāʼī's borrowings from earlier Arabic poetic tradition.
books.title_ar: الغيث المسجم في شرح لامية العجم
books.title_ur: الغیث المسجم فی شرح لامیۃ العجم

books.title: Sharḥ Lāmīyat al-ʻAjam (1429H)
books.evidence: Commentary likely analyzes al-Tughra'i's borrowings from earlier poetic traditions.

figures.name: Al-Safadi
figures.evidence: Al-Safadi documented poetic borrowings in his biographical dictionaries, providing secondary transmission of plagiarism analysis rather than original critical assessment.

figures.name: Al-Damiri
figures.evidence: Al-Damiri's zoological encyclopedia occasionally references poetic phrases but lacks systematic engagement with sariqat as critical practice.

concepts.definition_ar: التحليل النقدي لكيفية استعارة الشعراء اللاحقين للموضوعات والعبارات من السابقين.
concepts.definition_ur: بعد میں آنے والے شعراء کے پہلے والوں سے الفاظ اور خیالات لینے کا تنقیدی تجزیہ۔

concepts.name: Lafz and ma'na (word and meaning)
concepts.definition: Debate over whether eloquence resides in wording, meaning, or their composition.

books.title: The Book of Misers (Kitab al-Bukhala)
books.evidence: Mu'tazilite rationalist approach explores relationship between wording and meaning in discourse.

books.title: Exploits of the Turks
books.evidence: Balances stylistic ornament with substantive argument about Turkish virtues.

books.title: The Book of eloquence and demonstration
books.evidence: Jahiz debates whether eloquence resides in wording or meaning throughout.

books.title: Maqamat Badi' az-Zaman al-Hamadhani
books.evidence: Demonstrates mastery of both wording and meaning in rhetorical composition.

books.title: I‘jāz al-Qur’ān
books.evidence: Analyzes relationship between wording and meaning in Quranic eloquence.
books.author_name_ur: ابو بکر محمد بن عطیب باقلانی

books.title: The Diwan (Complete Poems) of al-Mutanabbi
books.evidence: His style exemplifies debate over whether wording or meaning carries eloquence.

books.title: Al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin (1926)
books.evidence: Analyzes relationship between wording and meaning in effective expression.

figures.name: Al-Jahiz
figures.evidence: Al-Jahiz's Kitab al-Hayawan extensively discusses eloquence, style, and meaning in Arabic language and rhetoric.

figures.name: Badi al-Zaman al-Hamadhani
figures.evidence: Al-Hamadhani's maqamat demonstrate linguistic virtuosity but less explicit theorization of lafz-ma'na debate.

figures.name: Al-Baqillani
figures.evidence: Al-Baqillani's I'jaz al-Qur'an directly addresses word-meaning composition in Qur'anic eloquence theory.

figures.name: Al-Mutanabbi
figures.evidence: Al-Mutanabbi's poetry exemplifies lafz-ma'na tensions but lacks theoretical framework for the debate itself.

concepts.definition_ar: جدل حول ما إذا كان الفضل اللغوي في الصيغة أو المعنى أو تركيبهما.
concepts.definition_ur: یہ بحث کہ بلاغت الفاظ میں ہے یا معنی میں یا ان کے امتزاج میں۔

concepts.name: Grammar versus logic debate
concepts.definition: The famous dispute over whether logic or Arabic grammar better captures meaning.

books.title: Al-Imtāʻ Wa-al-muʼānasah
books.evidence: Famous Night 8 debate between Matta and Sirafi on logic versus grammar centrally featured.

figures.name: Abū Hayyān al-Tawhīdī
figures.evidence: Al-Tawhīdī documented the logic-grammar debate in his Muqtabas but was not a primary disputant.

concepts.name_ur: منطق اور قواعد زبان کا تنازعہ
concepts.definition_ar: النزاع الشهير حول ما إذا كان المنطق أم النحو العربي أفضل لإدراك المعاني.
concepts.definition_ur: معنی کو سمجھنے میں منطق یا عربی قواعد میں کون بہتر ہے اس پر مشہور جھگڑا۔

concepts.name: Logic of language in usul
concepts.definition: Usul al-fiqh's analysis of command, prohibition, general, and particular as linguistic categories.

books.title: Al-Fauzul Kabeer Fee Usulit Tafseer
books.evidence: Usul al-tafsir typically treats linguistic categories of commands, general, particular in scripture.

books.title: Sharḥ al-Risālah al-waḍʻīyah al-ʻAḍudīyah li-ʻAlī Qūshjī
books.title_ar: شرح الرسالة الوضعية العضدية لعلي القوشجي
books.evidence: Qushji's commentary systematically explains linguistic categories of command, prohibition, and generality central to usul al-fiqh methodology.

figures.name: Shah Waliullah
figures.evidence: Shah Waliullah's Hujjat Allah al-Baligha systematically analyzes linguistic categories including command and prohibition in usul methodology.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Ali Qushji's primary work concerns astronomy and logic; no established connection to usul al-fiqh's language analysis documented.

concepts.definition_ar: تحليل أصول الفقه للأمر والنهي والعام والخاص كفئات لغوية.
concepts.definition_ur: اصول الفقہ کا امر، نہی، عام اور خاص کو لسانی زمرہ جات کے طور پر تجزیہ۔

concepts.name: 'Amm and khass as linguistic forms
concepts.definition: Analysis of general and particular expressions and their default semantic scope.
concepts.name_ur: عام اور خاص لسانی صورتوں کے طور پر
concepts.definition_ar: تحليل الصيغ العامة والخاصة وحدود مدلولاتها الدلالية الافتراضية.
concepts.definition_ur: عام اور خاص الفاظ اور ان کے پہلے سے طے شدہ معنی کی حدود کا تجزیہ۔

concepts.name: Mushtarak (homonymy)
concepts.definition: Words sharing a single form but carrying multiple unrelated meanings.
concepts.definition_ar: كلمات تتشارك في صيغة واحدة لكنها تحمل معانٍ متعددة لا علاقة بينها.
concepts.definition_ur: الفاظ جو ایک ہی صورت میں ہوں لیکن بالکل مختلف معنی رکھتے ہوں۔

concepts.name: Taraduf (synonymy)
concepts.definition: Debate over whether true synonyms exist in Arabic or every word carries distinct nuance.

books.title: Bedayiu'l-Lugat
books.evidence: Lexicographic works examining synonymy and lexical nuance in poetic vocabulary

figures.name: Ali Shir Nava'i
figures.evidence: Nava'i was Persian-Turkic poet; taraduf debate centers on Arabic linguistic theory, tangential connection.

concepts.definition_ar: جدل حول ما إذا كانت المترادفات الحقيقية موجودة في العربية أم لكل لفظ دقة خاصة.
concepts.definition_ur: یہ بحث کہ عربی میں حقیقی مترادفات ہیں یا ہر لفظ میں اپنی خصوصیت ہے۔

concepts.name: Furuq lughawiyya (lexical distinctions)
concepts.definition: Genre identifying subtle meaning differences between near-synonyms.

books.title: Bedayiu'l-Lugat
books.evidence: Arabic lexicography focused on subtle distinctions, core to the work's purpose

figures.name: Ali Shir Nava'i
figures.evidence: Nava'i was a poet and patron; no direct evidence he practiced or transmitted furuq lughawiyya specifically.

concepts.definition_ar: نوع من الدراسات اللغوية يكشف عن الفروق الدقيقة في المعاني بين الألفاظ القريبة.
concepts.definition_ur: قریب الرشتہ الفاظ کے درمیان معنی کے لطیف فروق کو ظاہر کرنے والی نوع۔

concepts.name: Addad (contranyms)
concepts.definition: Arabic words that carry two opposite meanings, catalogued as a lexical curiosity.

books.title: Pros and Cons
books.evidence: Al-Jahiz wrote on rhetoric and animals; no direct evidence this work catalogs Arabic contranyms systematically.

figures.name: Al-Jahiz
figures.evidence: Al-Jahiz documented Arabic lexical phenomena in his writings but was not primarily focused on addad as a specialized field.

concepts.definition_ar: ألفاظ عربية تحمل معنيين متضادين، وتُدرج كفضول لغوي.
concepts.definition_ur: عربی الفاظ جو دو متضاد معنیں رکھتے ہیں اور لغوی تجسس کے طور پر درج ہیں۔

concepts.name: Kitab al-'ayn system
concepts.definition: Al-Khalil's phonetic ordering of the lexicon by articulation point rather than alphabet.

books.title: Al-Fihrist
books.evidence: Documents al-Khalil's pioneering lexicographic work and phonetic ordering system.

books.title: Nakṯh al-Himyān fī Nukat al-ʿUmyān
books.evidence: Dictionary compilers among blind scholars feature prominently in biographical treatment.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nadim
figures.evidence: Ibn al-Nadim's Fihrist documents al-Khalil's lexicographic method and Kitab al-'ayn's phonetic ordering system directly.

figures.name: Al-Safadi
figures.evidence: Al-Safadi references al-Khalil and lexicographic traditions but provides secondary rather than primary documentation of the system.

concepts.definition_ar: ترتيب الخليل للمعجم الصوتي حسب مخرج النطق لا حسب الأبجدية.
concepts.definition_ur: خلیل کی لغت کی صوتی ترتیب کی بنیاد پر، نہ کہ حروف تہجی کی بنیاد پر۔

concepts.name: Rhyme-based lexicography
concepts.definition: Arranging dictionaries by the final radical to serve poets and rhymers.
concepts.definition_ar: ترتيب المعاجم حسب الحرف الأخير لخدمة الشعراء والموافقين.
concepts.definition_ur: شاعروں اور قافیہ بندوں کی خدمت کے لیے آخری حرف کے لحاظ سے لغات کا انتظام۔

concepts.name: Thematic lexicography
concepts.definition: Organizing vocabulary by semantic field such as camels, weapons, or weather.

books.title: Ṣifat Jazīrat al-ʻArab
books.evidence: Organizes vocabulary by geographic and tribal semantic fields systematically.

books.title: Dīwān ul-Lughat al-Turk
books.evidence: Organizes Turkic words by semantic fields following Arabic lexicographic tradition.

books.title: Muqaddimat al-Adab
books.evidence: Work organizes vocabulary by semantic fields rather than alphabetic order.

books.title: Ḥayāt al-ḥayawān al-kubrā
books.evidence: Organizes vocabulary by semantic field of animals, their names, traits, and behaviors.

books.title: Muʻjam mā astʻjm min Asmāʼ al-bilād wālmwāḍʻ (ʻĀlam al-Kutub, 1403h)
books.evidence: Organizes vocabulary by semantic field of geography and place names.
books.title_ar: معجم ما استُعجم من أسماء البلاد والمواضع
books.title_ur: معجم ما استعجم من اسماء البلاد والمواضع

figures.name: Al-Hamdani
figures.evidence: Al-Hamdani's geographical and lexicographical works organized knowledge by semantic regions and topical fields.

figures.name: Mahmud al-Kashgari
figures.evidence: Mahmud al-Kashgari's Divan organizes Turkish vocabulary systematically by semantic fields and thematic categories.

figures.name: Al-Zamakhshari
figures.evidence: Al-Zamakhshari's grammatical works include semantic organization but focus primarily on syntax and rhetoric.

figures.name: Al-Damiri
figures.evidence: Al-Damiri's Hayat al-Hayawan organizes animal vocabulary and knowledge by semantic zoological classification.

figures.name: Al-Bakri
figures.evidence: Al-Bakri's geographical dictionary organizes lexical entries by semantic regions and topical land classifications.

concepts.definition_ar: تنظيم المفردات حسب الحقل الدلالي كالإبل والسلاح والطقس.
concepts.definition_ur: الفاظ کو معنوی میدان کے لحاظ سے ترتیب دینا جیسے اونٹ، ہتھیار، اور موسم۔

concepts.name: Alfiyya commentary tradition
concepts.definition: Versified grammatical summas and the layered commentaries that explicate them.

books.title: Al-Lafẓ al-Jawharī fī radd khbāṭ al-Jūjarī
books.title_ar: اللفظ الجوهري في رد خبط الجوجري
books.title_ur: اللفظ الجوہری فی رد خبط الجوجری
books.evidence: Al-Suyuti's work addresses grammatical disputes but lacks direct engagement with Alfiyya verse commentary tradition structure.

figures.name: Al-Suyuti
figures.evidence: Al-Suyuti wrote commentaries on grammatical texts and transmitted Islamic scholarly traditions widely.

concepts.definition_ar: ملخصات نحوية موزونة والحواشي المتعددة التي توضحها.
concepts.definition_ur: منظوم نحوی خلاصے اور ان کی متعدد تشریحات۔

concepts.name: Persian grammatical tradition
concepts.definition: Grammar and lexicography of New Persian modeled on and distinguished from Arabic.

books.title: Muhakamat al-Lughatayn
books.evidence: Muhakamat directly compares Persian and Arabic grammar structures.

books.title: Bedayiu'l-Lugat
books.evidence: Nava'i wrote in Persian, documenting Persian lexicon alongside Arabic comparisons

figures.name: Ali Shir Nava'i
figures.evidence: Nava'i authored Muhakamatu'l-lughatayn, explicitly comparing Persian and Arabic grammatical structures.

concepts.definition_ar: نحو ومعجم الفارسية الحديثة المقتبس من العربية والمتميز عنها.
concepts.definition_ur: جدید فارسی کی نحو اور لغت جو عربی سے ماخوذ اور ممتاز ہے۔

concepts.name: Turkic lexicography
concepts.definition: Comparative documentation of Turkic dialects and vocabulary beginning with al-Kashgari.

books.title: Dīwān ul-Lughat al-Turk
books.evidence: First systematic Turkic lexicon and grammar, foundational to comparative documentation.

books.title: Muhakamat al-Lughatayn
books.evidence: Nava'i argues for Chagatai Turkish's superiority over Persian in lexical richness.

figures.name: Mahmud al-Kashgari
figures.evidence: Al-Kashgari's Diwān Lughāt al-Turk is the foundational comparative Turkic lexicographic work documenting dialects.

figures.name: Ali Shir Nava'i
figures.evidence: Nava'i wrote in Turkic and theorized vernacular language but compiled no systematic comparative lexicographic documentation.

concepts.definition_ar: توثيق مقارن للهجات والمفردات التركية بدءًا من الكاشغري.
concepts.definition_ur: ترکی بولیوں اور الفاظ کی موازنہ شدہ توثیق جو الکاشغری سے شروع ہوتی ہے۔

concepts.name: Fusha and 'ammiyya (standard and vernacular)
concepts.definition: Recognition of the gap between classical Arabic and spoken dialects.
concepts.definition_ar: الاعتراف بالفجوة بين العربية الكلاسيكية والعربية المنطوقة المحلية.
concepts.definition_ur: عربی فصحیٰ اور محلی بولی جانے والی عربی کے درمیان فاصلے کی شناخت۔

concepts.name: Saj' (rhymed prose)
concepts.definition: Ornate rhymed and rhythmic prose style characteristic of sermons and maqamat.

books.title: Sermon of the Roar of a Camel
books.evidence: As a sermon by Ali, likely employs ornate rhymed prose characteristic of early Arabic oratory.

books.title: The Book of Misers (Kitab al-Bukhala)
books.evidence: Employs ornate prose style characteristic of adab literature with rhetorical embellishment.

books.title: Maqamat Badi' az-Zaman al-Hamadhani
books.evidence: The Maqamat is the foundational work defining the maqama genre itself.

figures.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
figures.evidence: Ali's sermons influenced Arabic rhetoric but no direct evidence links him to saj' formalization.

figures.name: Al-Jahiz
figures.evidence: Al-Jahiz wrote extensively on rhetoric and style, including ornate prose techniques foundational to saj'.

figures.name: Badi al-Zaman al-Hamadhani
figures.evidence: Al-Hamadhani invented the maqama form, which is explicitly defined as characteristic of saj' rhymed prose.

concepts.definition_ar: أسلوب نثر موزون وموافق خصائص الخطب والمقامات.
concepts.definition_ur: منظوم اور موزوں نثر کا انداز جو خطبوں اور مقاموں کی خصوصیت ہے۔

concepts.name: Insha' (chancery prose)
concepts.definition: The art of official epistolary composition codified in chancery manuals.

books.title: al-Rasāʼil al-siyāsīyah
books.evidence: Political epistles exemplify official prose composition addressed to rulers and officials.

figures.name: Al-Jahiz
figures.evidence: Al-Jahiz wrote epistolary works and theoretical discussions on composition, but not primarily a chancery manual specialist.

concepts.definition_ar: فن تأليف الرسائل الرسمية المقنن في مناهج الديوان.
concepts.definition_ur: سرکاری خطوط کی تحریر کا فن جو دیوان کی ہدایات میں مقرر ہے۔

concepts.name: 'Ilm al-khatt (calligraphic theory)
concepts.definition: The aesthetic and proportional theory of Arabic script and its canonical hands.
concepts.definition_ar: النظرية الجمالية والنسبية لكتابة العربية وأشكالها القانونية.
concepts.definition_ur: عربی لکھاوٹ اور اس کی معیاری اقسام کے جمالیاتی اور تناسبی نظریہ۔

concepts.name: Rasm al-mushaf (Qur'anic orthography)
concepts.definition: The fixed consonantal spelling of the Qur'anic codex and its rules.

books.title: Koran Sharif (Part 1)
books.evidence: The consonantal text established under Zayd's compilation fixed the Uthmanic rasm.

books.title: Kor-an Sharif
books.evidence: Zayd ibn Thabit compiled the authoritative Quranic codex with fixed consonantal spelling.

figures.name: Zayd ibn Thabit
figures.evidence: Zayd ibn Thabit led official Qur'an compilation under Uthman, establishing standardized rasm al-mushaf orthography.

concepts.definition_ar: الإملاء الساكن الثابت للقرآن الكريم وقواعده.
concepts.definition_ur: قرآن کریم کی مقررہ تہجی اور اس کے اصول۔

concepts.name: Nahda Arabic reform
concepts.definition: 19th–20th century project to modernize Arabic vocabulary and simplify grammar.

books.title: Hak Dīni Kur'an Dili
books.evidence: 1942 modernist work engaging with contemporary Turkish language reform debates.

books.title: Tafsīr al-Qurʼān al-Ḥakīm (tafsīr al-Manār) (al-Hayʼah al-Miṣrīyah, 1990)
books.evidence: Reflects modernist linguistic sensibility in reformist Quranic commentary.

books.title: The genius of reform and education Imam Muhammad Abdu
books.title_ar: عبقري الإصلاح والتعليم: الإمام محمد عبده
books.evidence: Directly addresses Muhammad Abduh's reform thought and educational philosophy central to Nahda modernization project.

figures.name: Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
figures.evidence: Yazır's Qur'an tafsir employed modernized Arabic interpretation methods aligned with Nahda linguistic simplification.

figures.name: Rashid Rida
figures.evidence: Rida founded Al-Manar journal promoting Arabic language reform and modern Islamic thought central to Nahda.

figures.name: Abbas el-Akkad
figures.evidence: El-Akkad's philosophical writings used simplified, modernized Arabic vocabulary characteristic of Nahda reform movement.

concepts.definition_ar: مشروع القرن التاسع عشر والعشرين لتحديث المفردات العربية وتبسيط النحو.
concepts.definition_ur: انیسویں اور بیسویں صدی کا منصوبہ عربی الفاظ کو جدید بنانا اور نحو کو آسان کرنا۔

concepts.name: Sifat Allah (divine attributes)
concepts.definition: Whether God's attributes like knowledge and speech are real, metaphorical, or identical to His essence.

figures.name: Ibrahim al-Nazzam
figures.evidence: Argued attributes are identical to essence, not additional realities in divine being.

figures.name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
figures.evidence: Defended affirming divine attributes without ta'wil in opposition to Mu'tazili negation.

figures.name: Al-Mutawakkil
figures.evidence: Restored traditionalist affirmation of divine attributes after Mu'tazili suppression.

figures.name: Al-Tahawi
figures.evidence: Al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah affirms real divine attributes without anthropomorphism.

figures.name: Al-Jubba'i
figures.evidence: Argued God's attributes are identical to His essence, not additional eternal entities.

figures.name: Abu Mansur al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Affirmed real divine attributes distinct from essence against Mu'tazili ta'til in Kitab al-Tawhid.

figures.name: Al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Held divine attributes are real and eternal but distinct from essence in Kitab al-Tawhid.

figures.name: Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Al-Ibana defends real eternal divine attributes distinct from essence against Mu'tazili negation.

figures.name: Al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Defended real divine attributes distinct from essence against Mu'tazila in Al-Ibana.

figures.name: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Ahmad
figures.evidence: Argued divine attributes are identical to essence in Kitab al-Mughni.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Presents orthodox Sunni position on divine attributes in The Doctrine of the Sufis.

figures.name: Al-Baqillani
figures.evidence: Systematized Ash'ari doctrine of real eternal attributes in Tamhīd al-awāʼil.

figures.name: Abd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin Qushayri
figures.evidence: Al-Tahbir fi al-tazkir sharh Asmau al-Husna systematically treats divine names and attributes.

figures.name: Imam al-Juwayni
figures.evidence: Systematized Ash'ari position on divine attributes in al-Irshad fi Usul al-I'tiqad.

figures.name: Al-Baghawi
figures.evidence: Sharh al-Sunna transmits Ash'ari-Shafi'i positions on divine attributes.

figures.name: Ibn Tumart
figures.evidence: Rejected Ash'ari doctrine of real eternal attributes distinct from essence in Guiding Creed.

figures.name: Al-Shahrastani
figures.evidence: Documents debates on divine attributes across sects in Milal wa-al-nihal.

figures.name: Ibn al-Jawzi
figures.evidence: Upheld affirmation of attributes without tashbih in his theological writings.

figures.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
figures.evidence: Ithbat Sifat al-Ulu affirms divine attributes including elevation without metaphor.

figures.name: Fakhr al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Systematically treats divine attributes in Asas al-Taqdis reconciling reason with revelation.

figures.name: Al-Baydawi
figures.evidence: Tawali' al-Anwar systematizes Ash'ari doctrine on divine attributes as real and eternal.

figures.name: Al-Qurtubi
figures.evidence: Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna explicates the divine names and their theological implications.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Al-Risalah al-Arshiyya affirms real divine attributes against ta'til without tashbih.

figures.name: Al-Dhahabi
figures.evidence: Defended literalist position on divine attributes in Kitab al-'Uluw lil-'Ali al-Ghaffar.

figures.name: Al-Idji
figures.evidence: Developed Asharite doctrine of real attributes distinct from essence in al-Mawaqif.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Affirmed literal divine attributes following Ibn Taymiyya's approach in multiple works.

figures.name: Ibn Kathir
figures.evidence: Follows Ibn Taymiyya's affirmation of divine attributes without ta'wil in his tafsir.

figures.name: Al-Taftazani
figures.evidence: Systematically treated divine attributes in Sharh al-'Aqa'id al-Nasafiyya commentary.

figures.name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
figures.evidence: Maintains Hanbali affirmation of divine attributes without ta'wil in hadith commentaries.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Ash'ari theological definitions on divine attributes in Taʻrīfāt.

figures.name: Al-Laqqani
figures.evidence: Jawhara covers divine attributes following Ash'ari affirmation of real attributes.

figures.name: Nuruddin al-Raniri
figures.evidence: Defended Ash'ari position on divine attributes in theological works against philosophical Sufism.

figures.name: Al-Bajuri
figures.evidence: Explicates divine attributes following Ash'ari school in Tuhfat al-Murid.

figures.name: Mustafa Sabri Efendi
figures.evidence: Upheld traditional Ash'ari positions on divine attributes against rationalists.

figures.name: Abd al-Aziz Ibn Baz
figures.evidence: Affirmed literal divine attributes without ta'wil in Majmu' Fatawa.

concepts.definition_ar: هل صفات الله كالعلم والكلام حقيقية أم مجازية أم عين ذاته
concepts.definition_ur: کیا اللہ کی صفات جیسے علم اور کلام حقیقی ہیں یا عینِ ذات

concepts.name: Al-Manzila bayn al-Manzilatayn (intermediate position)
concepts.definition: Mu'tazili doctrine that a grave sinner is neither a believer nor an unbeliever.

figures.name: Zayd ibn Ali
figures.evidence: Adopted Mu'tazili position on grave sinners in his theological framework.

figures.name: Al-Jubba'i
figures.evidence: Transmitted classical Mu'tazili position on grave sinners' intermediate status.

figures.name: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Ahmad
figures.evidence: Elaborated intermediate status of grave sinner in Sharḥ al-uṣūl al-khamsah.

concepts.definition_ar: عقيدة المعتزلة بأن مرتكب الكبيرة ليس مؤمناً ولا كافراً
concepts.definition_ur: معتزلی عقیدہ کہ کبیرہ گناہ کا مرتکب نہ مومن ہے نہ کافر

concepts.name: Iman (definition of faith)
concepts.definition: Whether faith is inward assent, verbal profession, works, or all three combined.

figures.name: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
figures.evidence: First person to profess faith combining assent and public profession of Islam.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
figures.evidence: Exemplified prophetic definition of faith through immediate acceptance of Muhammad's message.

figures.name: Amr ibn al-As
figures.evidence: Early Companion who transmitted foundational understanding of faith from the Prophet's era.

figures.name: Masruq ibn al-Ajda
figures.evidence: Known to transmit early views on faith from Companions like Umar and Ibn Masud.

figures.name: Hasan al-Basri
figures.evidence: His definitions of faith as including works influenced Kharijite and Murji'ite debates.

figures.name: Jabir ibn Zayd
figures.evidence: Articulated that faith requires both belief and works, foundational to Ibadi theology.

figures.name: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani
figures.evidence: As Tabi'i scholar in Basra, transmitted early community teachings on faith's definition.

figures.name: Imam Abu Hanifa
figures.evidence: Defined faith as recognition and affirmation in Al-Fiqh al-Akbar, influencing Maturidi theology.

figures.name: Sufyan al-Thawri
figures.evidence: As ascetic teacher, transmitted early pietist understanding of faith from Kufa.

figures.name: Waki ibn al-Jarrah
figures.evidence: Known work 'Zuhd' reflects early pious tradition on faith and ascetic practice.

figures.name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
figures.evidence: Defined faith as statement, belief, and action in opposition to Murji'i minimalism.

figures.name: Imam al-Bukhari
figures.evidence: Sahih al-Bukhari includes Book of Faith defining iman through prophetic reports.

figures.name: Imam Muslim
figures.evidence: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman transmits prophetic definitions of faith and its components.

figures.name: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
figures.evidence: Sahih Muslim contains the Book of Faith (Kitab al-Iman) transmitting hadith on faith's definition.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Tirmidhi
figures.evidence: Transmitted hadiths on the definition of faith in his Jami' al-Tirmidhi.

figures.name: Al-Tahawi
figures.evidence: Al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah defines faith as assent, profession, and works combined.

figures.name: Abu Mansur al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Defined faith as tasdiq (assent) with works as completion not essence in Kitab al-Tawhid.

figures.name: Al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Defined faith as conviction and affirmation, with works as perfection not essence.

figures.name: Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Addressed definition of faith in Maqalat, mediating between Kharijite and Murji'ite extremes.

figures.name: Al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Treated faith as assent with verbal profession, allowing degrees, in Al-Ibana.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Defends Sufi understanding of faith as compatible with Sunni orthodoxy in his work.

figures.name: Al-Baghawi
figures.evidence: Sharh al-Sunna preserves traditional Sunni definition of faith as creed and works.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Iman defines faith as belief, speech, and deed, increasing and decreasing.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Discusses faith as belief, speech, and action in Madarij al-Salikin.

figures.name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
figures.evidence: Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam systematically treats faith's definition through hadith commentary.

figures.name: Al-Laqqani
figures.evidence: Jawhara defines faith following Ash'ari understanding.

figures.name: Bediuzzaman Said Nursi
figures.evidence: Risale-i Nur systematically explores certainty levels and rational foundations of faith.

figures.name: Malcolm X
figures.evidence: Redefined faith to include social justice action in 'The Ballot or the Bullet' speech.

figures.name: Fethullah Gülen
figures.evidence: Discusses definition and components of faith in The Essentials of the Islamic Faith.

concepts.definition_ar: هل الإيمان تصديق بالقلب أم إقرار باللسان أم عمل أم جميعها
concepts.definition_ur: کیا ایمان دل کی تصدیق ہے یا زبان کا اقرار یا عمل یا سب

concepts.name: Wujud and Mahiyya (existence and essence)
concepts.definition: Whether existence is really distinct from essence in created things, and what that implies for God.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Al-Amiri's al-Amad ala al-Abad treats essence-existence distinction in creatures.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Extended Avicennan metaphysics in his philosophical treatise Miftah al-Tibb.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Systematized essence-existence distinction in Al-Shifa, treating existence as accident of essence.

figures.name: Al-Shahrastani
figures.evidence: Treats existence-essence distinction philosophically in Nihaya al-iqdam.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Treats existence-essence through light metaphysics, prioritizing light over quiddity.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Advanced Avicennan metaphysics of existence-essence distinction in Tajrid al-I'tiqad.

figures.name: Muhammad ibn Muhammad Tabrizi
figures.evidence: 13th-century Persian philosopher likely engaged Avicennan metaphysics standard in his era.

figures.name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
figures.evidence: Integrated existence-essence distinction with mystical metaphysics in dialogue with philosophers.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Systematically treated existence-essence distinction in Hikmat al-Ishraq commentary.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Engaged Avicennan metaphysics in theological context following earlier Shia scholars.

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri
figures.evidence: Merged Avicennan metaphysics with Akbarian theosophy in his philosophical works.

figures.name: Al-Taftazani
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan metaphysical distinctions in theological context.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Kitāb al-taʻrīfāt provides canonical definitions distinguishing existence and essence.

figures.name: Ali ibn Mohammed al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Jurjani Definitions (Kitāb al-taʻrīfāt) provides technical definitions of philosophical terms including essence.

figures.name: Molla Fenari
figures.evidence: Studied under Dawud al-Kayseri, key transmitter of Ibn Arabi's ontology to Ottoman realm.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Extended debates on existence-essence distinction in his commentaries on Ibn Sina and Tusi.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: Combined Avicennan essence-existence with Illuminationist metaphysics in Mujli al-Ahzan.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Developed theory of huduth dahri (perpetual origination) in Qabasat reconciling essence and existence.

figures.name: Mir Fendereski
figures.evidence: Engaged existence-essence distinction in his metaphysical works bridging traditions.

figures.name: Mulla Sadra
figures.evidence: Resolves existence-essence debate by prioritizing existence in Hikmat al-Muta'aliya.

figures.name: Rajab Ali Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Worked on existence-essence distinction as part of Sadrian philosophical tradition.

figures.name: Qazi Sa’id Qumi
figures.evidence: Qumi wrote extensively on existence-essence distinction in his philosophical commentaries.

figures.name: Abdu Al Rahim Damavandi
figures.evidence: Core metaphysical distinction taught in 18th-century Iranian philosophical curriculum.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Extensively treated existence-essence distinction in his Manzuma philosophical poem.

figures.name: Allameh Sayyed Abul Hasan Rafiee Qazvini
figures.evidence: As traditional Iranian philosopher, would have taught Avicennan distinction in Qazvin seminary.

figures.name: Mirza Mahdi Elahi Qomshehei
figures.evidence: As Isfahan school philosopher, likely engaged existence-essence debates central to that tradition.

figures.name: Muhammad Husayn Tabatabaei
figures.evidence: Developed existence-essence distinction following Mulla Sadra in philosophical works.

figures.name: Mohammad-Taqi Ja'fari
figures.evidence: Major contributions to ontological debates on existence-essence distinction in Islamic philosophy.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Engaged deeply with existence-essence distinction in his works on Islamic philosophy.

figures.name: Nasrollah Hekmat
figures.evidence: Contemporary Islamic philosopher in Tehran engaging foundational metaphysical distinctions.

figures.name: Ali Asghar Mosleh
figures.evidence: Active in Iranian philosophical debates on existence-essence distinction.

concepts.definition_ar: هل الوجود مغاير حقاً للماهية في الممكنات وما يترتب على ذلك في حق الله
concepts.definition_ur: کیا ممکنات میں وجود ماہیت سے حقیقتاً الگ ہے

concepts.name: Wajib and Mumkin (necessary and contingent being)
concepts.definition: Dividing all that exists into what must exist in itself and what might or might not.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Formulated necessary-contingent division and proof of God in Al-Najat and Al-Isharat.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Systematized necessary-contingent being distinction in Tajrid al-I'tiqad.

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri
figures.evidence: Integrated necessary-contingent distinction into Akbarian ontology.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Definitions text systematizes necessary versus contingent being distinction.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Systematized necessary-contingent distinction in his metaphysics throughout al-Rawashih al-Samawiyya.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Refined necessary-contingent being analysis in his systematic philosophical works.

concepts.definition_ar: تقسيم الموجودات إلى ما يجب وجوده بذاته وما يجوز وجوده وعدمه
concepts.definition_ur: موجودات کی تقسیم واجب الوجود اور ممکن الوجود میں

concepts.name: Al-Aql al-Fa'al (Active Intellect)
concepts.definition: The cosmic intellect that actualizes human thought and grants prophetic knowledge.

figures.name: Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi
figures.evidence: Referenced cosmic intellect mediating celestial influences in his theory of astral causation.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: On the Intellect first introduces Active Intellect doctrine into Arabic philosophy.

figures.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
figures.evidence: Integrated Active Intellect into Ismaili cosmology as source of prophetic knowledge.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Detailed Active Intellect as agent of human knowledge in epistemology and politics.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Discussed Active Intellect's role in illuminating human souls in al-Muntakhab Siwan al-Hikma.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Used Active Intellect theory in explaining prophetic knowledge and human intellection.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Developed Active Intellect as source of human intellection in De Anima of Al-Shifa.

figures.name: Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din al-Shirazi
figures.evidence: Discussed Active Intellect's role in cosmology throughout his philosophical treatises.

figures.name: Nasir Khusraw
figures.evidence: Integrates Active Intellect into Ismaili cosmology of universal intellect and soul.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Tadbir al-Mutawahhid develops theory of conjunction with Active Intellect for human perfection.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy achieves union with Active Intellect as climax of rational ascent.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Rejected Avicenna's separate Active Intellect in unity of the intellect treatise.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Recasts Active Intellect as Lord of Species in illuminationist cosmology.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Treated Active Intellect theory in his synthesis of peripatetic thought.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Discusses Active Intellect in philosophical commentaries following Avicenna.

concepts.definition_ar: العقل الكوني الذي يُفعّل الفكر الإنساني ويمنح المعرفة النبوية
concepts.definition_ur: وہ کونیاتی عقل جو انسانی فکر کو فعال کرتی ہے

concepts.name: Nafs Natiqa (the rational soul)
concepts.definition: The immaterial human soul in Avicennan philosophy, its faculties and survival after death.

figures.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
figures.evidence: Transmitted Neoplatonic psychology of rational soul in Ismaili framework.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated and wrote 'The Difference between Spirit and Soul' on Galenic psychology.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Treated rational soul's faculties in his psychology, pre-Avicennan framework.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Explored rational soul's nature and immortality in his philosophical anthology.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Developed theory of rational soul in philosophical works on happiness and human perfection.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Treats rational soul's immortality in psychological works following Aristotle.

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi
figures.evidence: Discussed psychology of the rational soul extensively in al-Imta wa-l-Mu'anasa.

figures.name: Miskawayh
figures.evidence: Tahdhib al-Akhlaq analyzes rational soul's faculties and moral development.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan psychology through his medical and philosophical works.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Refined rational soul theory and floating man argument for soul's independence in Al-Shifa.

figures.name: Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din al-Shirazi
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan psychology within Isma'ili philosophical framework.

figures.name: Nasir Khusraw
figures.evidence: Discusses rational soul within Ismaili philosophical anthropology in prose works.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Risala fi al-Nafs details rational soul's ascent from material to intellectual actualization.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy ibn Yaqzan traces soul's self-development from isolation to rational perfection.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Challenged Avicennan individual soul immortality in unity of intellect works.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Treats rational soul through light ontology in Philosophy of Illumination.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Discussed rational soul doctrine in his philosophical encyclopedia.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Refined Avicennan psychology in his philosophical works on the rational soul.

figures.name: Mulla Sadra
figures.evidence: Treats soul's transubstantial motion in Kasr al-asnam al-jahiliyyah.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Covered Avicennan rational soul doctrine in his philosophical teaching.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Covered Avicennan psychology in his teaching of Islamic peripatetic philosophy.

concepts.definition_ar: النفس الإنسانية المجردة في الفلسفة الابن سينوية وقواها وبقاؤها بعد الموت
concepts.definition_ur: ابن سینا کی فلسفے میں مجرد انسانی روح اور اس کی قوتیں

concepts.name: Ishraq (illuminationism)
concepts.definition: Suhrawardi's philosophy of light as fundamental reality and knowledge as presence.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy's mystical illumination echoes earlier illuminationist philosophical themes.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Founded illuminationist philosophy in 'Philosophy of Illumination' (Hikmat al-Ishraq).

figures.name: Ibn Sab'in
figures.evidence: Known as Shaykh al-Ishraq al-Gharbi, reviving illuminationism in the West.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Al-Shahrazuri wrote extensive commentaries on Suhrawardi's illuminationist works.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Wrote major commentary on Suhrawardi's Hikmat al-Ishraq.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Transmitted Suhrawardi's illuminationist texts to his students in Shiraz school.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardi's Illuminationism with Peripatetic philosophy in his synthesis.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardian illuminationist themes with Peripatetic metaphysics in Isfahan school.

figures.name: Mir Fendereski
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardi's illuminationism with Peripatetic philosophy in his philosophical system.

figures.name: Rajab Ali Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Combined illuminationist themes with Sadrian metaphysics in Isfahan tradition.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Integrated illuminationist elements with Sadraean philosophy in his synthesis.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Taught Suhrawardi's illuminationist philosophy alongside Sadrian thought.

figures.name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
figures.evidence: Discusses Suhrawardi's illuminationism extensively in Three Muslim Sages.

figures.name: Nasrollah Pourjavady
figures.evidence: As Tehran philosophy scholar, translates illuminationist texts into Persian context.

figures.name: Nasrollah Hekmat
figures.evidence: Iranian philosopher likely exposed to Suhrawardian illuminationist currents in Tehran.

concepts.definition_ar: فلسفة السهروردي في النور كحقيقة أساسية والمعرفة كحضور
concepts.definition_ur: سہروردی کا فلسفہ نور بطور بنیادی حقیقت اور معرفت بطور حضور

concepts.name: Mantiq (logic)
concepts.definition: The Aristotelian syllogistic apparatus naturalized into Islamic scholarly curricula.

figures.name: Ibn al-Muqaffa
figures.evidence: Translated Persian works incorporating Aristotelian logic into Arabic intellectual culture.

figures.name: Ma'mun al-Rashid
figures.evidence: Sponsored translation of Aristotle's Organon into Arabic at Bayt al-Hikma.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: Die philosophischen Abhandlungen transmits Aristotelian logic to Arabic scholarship.

figures.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
figures.evidence: Translated Aristotle's Organon and Porphyry's Isagoge, making Greek logic available in Arabic.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated Aristotelian logical works as part of Greek-Arabic translation movement.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Wrote extensive commentaries on Aristotle's Organon, naturalized logic into Islamic curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Preserved and transmitted Aristotelian logic in Baghdad philosophical circle's curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi
figures.evidence: Engaged Aristotelian logic in al-Muqabasat and debates with Abu Sulayman al-Sijistani.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nadim
figures.evidence: Al-Fihrist catalogues logical works and translators of Greek logic into Arabic.

figures.name: Abū Hayyān al-Tawhīdī
figures.evidence: Studied logic under Yahya ibn Adi, a leading Aristotelian logician of Baghdad.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Systematized Aristotelian logic in works taught to later Persian scholars.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Systematized Aristotelian logic in Al-Shifa and Al-Isharat for Islamic philosophy curriculum.

figures.name: Ibn al-Sīd al-Baṭalyawsī
figures.evidence: As Andalusian philosopher trained in falsafa tradition, engaged Aristotelian logical methods.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Mantiq transmits Aristotelian logic to Andalusian philosophical tradition.

figures.name: Fakhr al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Mulahhas fi l-hikma wal-mantiq transmits Aristotelian logic systematically.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Commentary on Avicenna's Isharat transmitted Peripatetic logic to later generations.

figures.name: Al-Baydawi
figures.evidence: Tawali' al-Anwar employs Aristotelian logical methods in theological argumentation.

figures.name: Muhammad ibn Muhammad Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Aristotelian logic was core curriculum for Islamic philosophers in Tabriz by 13th century.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Included logical treatises in his comprehensive philosophical works.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Treated Aristotelian logic in philosophical commentaries.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Employed Aristotelian logic systematically in theological argumentation and jurisprudence.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
