figures.evidence: Naqd al-Mantiq systematically refutes Aristotelian logic as unnecessary for Islamic sciences.

figures.name: Al-Idji
figures.evidence: Advanced logical theory in al-Risala al-Wad'iyya on linguistic conventions.

figures.name: Al-Taftazani
figures.evidence: Produced major commentaries on logic including works on Aristotelian syllogistics.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah incorporates Aristotelian logic in methodology of historical analysis.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Ḥāshiyat on Shamsīyah systematizes Aristotelian logic for Islamic curriculum.

figures.name: Ali ibn Mohammed al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Ḥāshiyat ʻalá taṣawwurāt sharḥ al-Risālah al-shamsīyah fī al-qawāʻid al-manṭiqīyah is a commentary on logic.

figures.name: Molla Fenari
figures.evidence: Wrote glosses on logic texts, establishing Ottoman madrasa curriculum in Bursa.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Sharh al-Risalah al-Wadiyah treats Aristotelian logic for theological students.

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.evidence: Studied philosophy under scholars like George Scholarius and established madrasas teaching logic.

figures.name: Qazi Sa’id Qumi
figures.evidence: Taught Aristotelian logic as part of standard philosophical curriculum in Qom.

figures.name: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi
figures.evidence: Islamic sciences scholar in Ottoman tradition taught Aristotelian logic as standard curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Bajuri
figures.evidence: AuthoredHashiyaÊ» ala Sharh al-Sullam, a commentary on Akhdarī's logic text.

figures.name: Abbasgulu Bakikhanov
figures.evidence: As philosopher, likely engaged Aristotelian logic common in 19th-century curricula.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Taught Aristotelian logic as foundation of his philosophical curriculum.

figures.name: Mohammad-Taqi Ja'fari
figures.evidence: Taught and transmitted Aristotelian logic within Islamic philosophical curriculum at Tabriz.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Taught traditional Aristotelian logic as part of philosophical training in Qom.

concepts.definition_ar: الجهاز القياسي الأرسطي الذي تبنّته المناهج العلمية الإسلامية
concepts.definition_ur: ارسطو کی قیاسی منطق جو اسلامی علمی نصاب میں شامل ہوئی

concepts.name: Sa'ada (philosophical happiness)
concepts.definition: The ultimate end of human life conceived as intellectual and moral perfection.

figures.name: Ibn al-Muqaffa
figures.evidence: Transmitted Persian philosophical ethics on virtuous life in his Adab al-Kabir.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Defined happiness as ultimate intellectual perfection in Tahsil al-Sa'ada.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Discussed philosophical happiness as ultimate end in his ethical writings.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Central theme in his al-I'lam bi-Manaqib al-Islam, treating happiness as philosophical end.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Al-Sa'ada wa al-Is'ad synthesizes Aristotelian and Islamic views on ultimate happiness.

figures.name: Miskawayh
figures.evidence: Systematized virtue ethics in Tahdhib al-Akhlaq, defining happiness as soul perfection.

figures.name: Abū Hayyān al-Tawhīdī
figures.evidence: Discusses philosophical happiness and human fulfillment in his salon dialogues.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.evidence: Rubaiyat explores earthly pleasure and philosophical contentment as human fulfillment themes.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Tadbir al-Mutawahhid presents solitary philosopher's path to intellectual happiness via contemplation.

figures.name: Nizami Ganjavi
figures.evidence: Khamsa integrates philosophical happiness with mystical love and ethical virtue.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Merged philosophical ethics with Persian tradition in Akhlaq-i Nasiri.

figures.name: Abbas el-Akkad
figures.evidence: Examined human excellence and genius through biographical studies of historical exemplars.

figures.name: Mohammed Aziz Lahbabi
figures.evidence: Reinterpreted philosophical happiness through personalist lens of authentic self-realization.

concepts.definition_ar: الغاية القصوى للحياة الإنسانية بوصفها كمالاً عقلياً وأخلاقياً
concepts.definition_ur: انسانی زندگی کا حتمی مقصد بطور عقلی اور اخلاقی کمال

concepts.name: Maslaha (public welfare)
concepts.definition: Using the common good as a criterion for legal rulings where texts are silent.

figures.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
figures.evidence: Suspended hudud penalty for theft during famine citing public welfare considerations.

figures.name: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
figures.evidence: Policy reforms prioritized public welfare, returning confiscated properties to original owners.

figures.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
figures.evidence: Al-Muwatta incorporates public welfare considerations in juridical reasoning alongside textual sources.

figures.name: Abu Yusuf
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Kharaj applies public welfare considerations to taxation and land policy.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qasim
figures.evidence: Transmitted Malik's consideration of public welfare in legal derivation.

figures.name: Sahnun
figures.evidence: Transmitted Maliki public welfare considerations in Al-Mudawwana's practical rulings.

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Integrated public welfare considerations into political theory in Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyyah.

figures.name: Nizam al-Mulk
figures.evidence: Siyasatnama grounds governance in public welfare and preservation of order under shariah.

figures.name: Imam al-Juwayni
figures.evidence: Advanced public interest considerations in legal theory in al-Ghiyathi.

figures.name: Nur al-Din Zangi
figures.evidence: Promoted public welfare through hospitals, madrasas, and infrastructure projects.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah grounds governance in societal welfare through concept of asabiyyah.

figures.name: Al-Wansharisi
figures.evidence: Fatwas in al-Mi'yar frequently invoke maslaha in cases of intercommunal relations and governance.

figures.name: Al-Hajj Salim Suwari
figures.evidence: Advocated patient da'wa over jihad based on public welfare considerations.

figures.name: Ebussuud Efendi
figures.evidence: Applied public welfare considerations in fatawa addressing Ottoman state needs.

figures.name: Rifa'a at-Tahtawi
figures.evidence: Argued for adopting European sciences and institutions based on public welfare.

figures.name: Muhammad Abduh
figures.evidence: Used public welfare principle as Grand Mufti for modernizing legal rulings.

figures.name: Al-Kawakibi
figures.evidence: Invoked public welfare to justify political reforms in Arab lands against Ottoman rule.

figures.name: Qasim Amin
figures.evidence: Argued women's unveiling and education serve public welfare in modernizing Egypt.

figures.name: Tahir ibn Ashur
figures.evidence: Integrated maslaha into maqasid framework in Maqasid al-Shariah al-Islamiyya.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: Extensively applied public welfare considerations in modern fatwa contexts across his work.

figures.name: Abdurrahman Wahid
figures.evidence: Invoked public welfare to justify inter-religious harmony and democratic governance.

figures.name: Fethullah Gulen
figures.evidence: Grounds Hizmet movement's educational and social projects in public welfare principles.

figures.name: Ziauddin Sardar
figures.evidence: Emphasized public welfare considerations in writings on Islamic futures and social reform.

concepts.definition_ar: اعتبار المنفعة العامة معياراً للأحكام حيث تسكت النصوص
concepts.definition_ur: عوامی بھلائی کو معیار بنانا جہاں نصوص خاموش ہوں

concepts.name: Al-Ahkam al-Khamsa (the five legal values)
concepts.definition: Classifying acts as obligatory, recommended, neutral, disliked, or forbidden.

figures.name: Shurayh al-Qadi
figures.evidence: Applied five-fold classification in judgments under Umar and Ali's guidance.

figures.name: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
figures.evidence: Issued legal classifications on pilgrimage rituals as Imam al-Hajj in Mecca.

figures.name: Abd al-Rahman al-Awza'i
figures.evidence: Early systematizer of legal classifications in Syrian juristic tradition before Hanafi-Shafi'i.

figures.name: Abu Dawud
figures.evidence: Structured Sunan Abu Dawud by legal categories mapping to the five-fold classification.

figures.name: Ibn Majah
figures.evidence: Sunan organized topically by legal rulings across ritual and civil matters.

figures.name: Al-Qabisi
figures.evidence: Classified legal rulings using five-value schema in educational writings.

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Applied five legal values framework throughout his juridical works.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Mabsut systematically categorizes acts into five legal values across all jurisprudential domains.

figures.name: Al-Qurtubi
figures.evidence: Jami' li-ahkam al-Qur'an systematically extracts legal rulings from Quranic verses.

figures.name: Yahya ibn Sharif al-Nawawi
figures.evidence: Riyad al-Salihin systematically organizes legal-ethical categories of actions.

figures.name: Al-Damiri
figures.evidence: al-Najm al-wahhāj fī sharḥ al-Minhāj is a commentary on Shafi'i legal methodology.

figures.name: Shaykh Bahai
figures.evidence: Jame-e Abbasi extensively treats Islamic ritual law and juridical classifications.

figures.name: Al-Bajuri
figures.evidence: Transmitted Shafi'i legal taxonomy in his fiqh works and teaching.

concepts.definition_ar: تصنيف الأفعال إلى واجب ومندوب ومباح ومكروه وحرام
concepts.definition_ur: افعال کی تقسیم واجب، مندوب، مباح، مکروہ اور حرام میں

concepts.name: Marja'iyya (source of emulation)
concepts.definition: Shia institution by which lay believers follow the rulings of a senior living jurist.

figures.name: Shah Abbas I
figures.evidence: Patronized ulama hierarchy that strengthened institutional Shia marja system in Iran.

figures.name: Hashim Larijani
figures.evidence: Held position as Grand Ayatollah and source of emulation for Shia believers.

figures.name: Ayatollah Khomeini
figures.evidence: Merged traditional marja role with political governance in founding Islamic Republic.

figures.name: Reza Zanjani
figures.evidence: Iranian cleric in 20th century would engage Shia source of emulation institution.

figures.name: Taqi Tabatabaei Qomi
figures.evidence: Served as marja al-taqlid with followers emulating his juristic rulings in Mashhad.

figures.name: Ahmad Azari Qomi
figures.evidence: As Qom-based cleric, participated in institution of lay believers following senior jurists.

figures.name: Yousef Madani Tabrizi
figures.evidence: As grand ayatollah served as source of emulation for Shia community in Tabriz region.

figures.name: Abbas Vaez-Tabasi
figures.evidence: Served as custodian of Imam Reza shrine, institutional role in Shia religious authority.

figures.name: Ali Mohammad Dastgheib Shirazi
figures.evidence: As Shirazi mystic in Shia context, would have operated within marja'iyya system.

figures.name: Ali Asghar Rahimi Azad
figures.evidence: As grand ayatollah, directly participated in marja institution as source of emulation.

figures.name: Ahmad Ghabel
figures.evidence: Mystic perspective likely challenged institutional clerical authority structures in Shia context.

figures.name: Hassan Khomeini
figures.evidence: Operates within Qom's marja'iyya system though not yet a marja himself.

figures.name: Muqtada al-Sadr
figures.evidence: Established alternative authority structure through Sadr movement challenging traditional hierarchy.

concepts.definition_ar: مؤسسة شيعية يتبع فيها العوام أحكام مرجع التقليد الحي
concepts.definition_ur: شیعہ ادارہ جس میں عوام مرجعِ تقلید کے احکام کی پیروی کرتے ہیں

concepts.name: Maqamat (stations on the path)
concepts.definition: Progressive moral and spiritual levels attained by the seeker's own effort.

figures.name: Abu Sulayman al-Darani
figures.evidence: Distinguished stations of the path, especially tawba, zuhd, and tawakkul in his teachings.

figures.name: Harith al-Muhasibi
figures.evidence: Among first to systematize spiritual stations in structured form for Sufi path development.

figures.name: Dhul-Nun al-Misri
figures.evidence: Pioneered the systematic classification of spiritual stations in early Sufism.

figures.name: Sari al-Saqati
figures.evidence: Among first Baghdad mystics to articulate progressive spiritual stations framework.

figures.name: Junayd of Baghdad
figures.evidence: Defined and systematized the progressive spiritual stations of the Sufi path.

figures.name: Ibn Khafif
figures.evidence: Transmitted Khorasan School's systematic teaching on spiritual stations.

figures.name: Al-Sarraj al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Systematized spiritual stations in Kitab al-Luma, first encyclopedic treatment of Sufi stages.

figures.name: Abu Talib al-Makki
figures.evidence: Qut al-Qulub systematizes spiritual stations along the Sufi path to God.

figures.name: Abu Nasr al-Sarraj
figures.evidence: Codified stations of the path systematically in Kitab al-Luma.

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur
figures.evidence: Catalogued progressive spiritual stations in Tabaqat al-Sufiyya systematically.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Systematizes stations of the Sufi path following Junayd in The Doctrine of the Sufis.

figures.name: Al-Qushayri
figures.evidence: al-Risala systematically catalogs spiritual stations from repentance through trust.

figures.name: Abd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin Qushayri
figures.evidence: Al-Risala al-Qushayriyya systematically organizes and defines spiritual stations (maqamat).

figures.name: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari
figures.evidence: Systematizes hundred spiritual stations in Manazil al-Sa'irin.

figures.name: Ali al-Hujwiri
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Mahjub systematizes the progressive spiritual stations of the Sufi path.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Hamadani
figures.evidence: Systematized progressive spiritual stations for disciples in Central Asian context.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.evidence: Systematized Sufi stations throughout the four quarters of Ihya Ulum al-Din.

figures.name: Abdul Qadir al-Jilani
figures.evidence: Al-Ghunya systematizes spiritual stations progressing from repentance to union.

figures.name: Abu Najib Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: His Adab al-Muridin systematically outlines spiritual stations for seekers on the path.

figures.name: Abdul Khaliq Ghujdawani
figures.evidence: Transmitted Khwajagan lineage's spiritual stations system from teacher Yusuf al-Hamadani.

figures.name: Ahmad al-Rifai
figures.evidence: Taught progressive spiritual stations within Suhrawardi tradition he inherited.

figures.name: Farid ud-Din Attar
figures.evidence: Conference of the Birds structures journey through seven valleys as progressive stations.

figures.name: Najm al-Din Kubra
figures.evidence: Detailed progressive stations framework in Kubrawiyya spiritual training methodology.

figures.name: Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Systematized spiritual stations and their progression in Awarif al-Ma'arif.

figures.name: Abu Hafs Umar al-Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Elaborated spiritual stations systematically in Awarif ul-Maarif for Sufi practitioners.

figures.name: Najm al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Explicates Kubrawiyya spiritual stations following his master Najmuddin Kubra's schema.

figures.name: Hajji Bektash Veli
figures.evidence: Four Doors structures spiritual path in four stages/doors combining Sufi station theory.

figures.name: Sharaf al-Din Maneri
figures.evidence: Systematically taught progressive spiritual stations in his epistolary guidance to disciples.

figures.name: Amir Kulal
figures.evidence: Guided disciples through spiritual stations as primary teacher of Naqshband lineage.

figures.name: Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani
figures.evidence: Transmitted Kubrawi understanding of spiritual stations through his extensive correspondence and teaching.

figures.name: Baha-ud-Din Naqshband
figures.evidence: Taught progressive spiritual stations through his principle of khalwat dar anjuman.

figures.name: Gesu Daraz
figures.evidence: Systematized Chishti stages of spiritual development in his treatises on suluk.

figures.name: Ibn Abbad al-Rundi
figures.evidence: Maps spiritual stations in his guidance letters to disciples on the Sufi path.

figures.name: Ali ibn Wafa
figures.evidence: Guided disciples through spiritual stations as Shadhili master in Cairo.

figures.name: Yahya al-Shirvani
figures.evidence: Systematized stations of the path for Khalwatiyya initiates following classical Sufi models.

figures.name: Ahmad Zarruq
figures.evidence: Transmitted classical Shadhili station doctrine through his Sufi writings.

figures.name: Shaykh Zarruq
figures.evidence: Detailed spiritual stations in his systematic works on Sufi path and practice.

figures.name: Bali Efendi
figures.evidence: Naqshbandi instruction involved guiding disciples through spiritual stations.

figures.name: Muhammad Ghaus Gwaliari
figures.evidence: Detailed progressive stations in Shattariyya path in his works.

figures.name: Aziz Mahmud Hudayi
figures.evidence: Outlined spiritual stations in his guidance texts for disciples.

figures.name: Khwaja Baqi Billah
figures.evidence: Taught classical Sufi stations through Naqshbandi training methodology in Delhi.

figures.name: Mirza Mazhar Jan-e-Janan
figures.evidence: Instructed disciples on progressive stations following Naqshbandi-Mujaddidi framework.

figures.name: Syed Ahmad Kabir Rifai
figures.evidence: Suhrawardiyya systematizes spiritual stations; transmitted as Bengali tariqa master.

figures.name: Ashraf Ali Thanvi
figures.evidence: Detailed spiritual stations in his Sufi manuals following classical Chishti taxonomy.

concepts.definition_ar: مراتب أخلاقية وروحية يبلغها السالك بجهده الخاص
concepts.definition_ur: اخلاقی اور روحانی منازل جو سالک اپنی محنت سے حاصل کرے

concepts.name: Ahwal (spiritual states)
concepts.definition: Transient God-given conditions experienced on the path, distinct from earned stations.

figures.name: Dhul-Nun al-Misri
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient spiritual states (ahwal) from permanent stations (maqamat).

figures.name: Junayd of Baghdad
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient God-given states from stable earned stations in Sufi doctrine.

figures.name: Abu al-Husayn al-Nuri
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from stations under his teacher Junayd's guidance.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Shibli
figures.evidence: Exemplified transient God-given states through his famous ecstatic episodes in Baghdad.

figures.name: Ibn Khafif
figures.evidence: Preserved distinction between stations and states in Khorasan tradition.

figures.name: Al-Sarraj al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from stations in Kitab al-Luma, foundational for later Sufism.

figures.name: Abu Talib al-Makki
figures.evidence: Qut al-Qulub distinguishes transient spiritual states from earned stations.

figures.name: Abu Nasr al-Sarraj
figures.evidence: Distinguished states from stations in Kitab al-Luma's systematic framework.

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur
figures.evidence: Preserved early Khorasani teachings on transient spiritual states in biographical collections.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Codifies distinction between stations and states in The Doctrine of the Sufis.

figures.name: Al-Qushayri
figures.evidence: al-Risala distinguishes transient states from earned stations as key Sufi taxonomy.

figures.name: Abd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin Qushayri
figures.evidence: Al-Risala al-Qushayriyya distinguishes transient states (ahwal) from earned stations.

figures.name: Ali al-Hujwiri
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Mahjub distinguishes transient God-given states from earned stations on the path.

figures.name: Abu Najib Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Adab al-Muridin distinguishes transient states from earned stations in Sufi practice.

figures.name: Najm al-Din Kubra
figures.evidence: Mapped transient mystical states through colored lights phenomenon in visionary experience.

figures.name: Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from permanent stations in his Sufi teachings.

figures.name: Abu Hafs Umar al-Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from permanent stations in Awarif ul-Maarif.

figures.name: Najm al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Distinguishes transient states from stations in The Path of God's Bondsmen.

concepts.definition_ar: حالات روحية عابرة يهبها الله في الطريق تختلف عن المقامات المكتسبة
concepts.definition_ur: اللہ کی عطا کردہ عارضی روحانی کیفیات جو مکتسب مقامات سے مختلف ہیں

concepts.name: Ma'rifa (gnosis)
concepts.definition: Direct tasting knowledge of God beyond discursive reasoning.

figures.name: Ja'far al-Sadiq
figures.evidence: Taught direct spiritual knowledge of God to Sufi disciples including Jabir ibn Hayyan.

figures.name: Ma'ruf al-Karkhi
figures.evidence: Distinguished experiential gnosis from discursive knowledge in Baghdad teaching.

figures.name: Harith al-Muhasibi
figures.evidence: Works integrate direct experiential knowledge of God within theological orthodoxy.

figures.name: Dhul-Nun al-Misri
figures.evidence: First to systematically articulate ma'rifa as direct gnosis distinct from rational knowledge.

figures.name: Sari al-Saqati
figures.evidence: Taught direct knowledge of God through states, influenced Junayd's gnosis doctrine.

figures.name: Abu Yazid al-Bistami
figures.evidence: Central figure in Khorasan school's development of experiential gnosis of God.

figures.name: Sahl al-Tustari
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct mystical knowledge of God in his Qur'an commentary.

figures.name: Hakim al-Tirmidhi
figures.evidence: Distinguished gnosis from learned knowledge in multiple works on spiritual epistemology.

figures.name: Junayd of Baghdad
figures.evidence: Taught direct experiential knowledge of God within framework of legal orthodoxy.

figures.name: Ibn Masarra
figures.evidence: Combined philosophical and mystical approaches to direct knowledge of God in his teachings.

figures.name: Abu Talib al-Makki
figures.evidence: Qut al-Qulub treats gnosis as direct experiential knowledge beyond reason.

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi
figures.evidence: Bridged philosophical epistemology with mystical knowledge in al-Muqabasat discussions.

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur
figures.evidence: Transmitted Khorasani teachings on gnosis in his extensive Sufi biographical works.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Integrates Sufi gnosis with Sunni theology in The Doctrine of the Sufis.

figures.name: Abu al-Hasan Kharaqani
figures.evidence: Titled Sultan al-Arifin (King of Gnostics), teaching direct knowledge of God.

figures.name: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari
figures.evidence: Discusses gnosis as culminating station in mystical path of Manazil.

figures.name: Ali al-Hujwiri
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Mahjub emphasizes direct gnosis of God as the goal of the mystical journey.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.evidence: Combined juridical knowledge with mystical gnosis in Mishkat al-Anwar and Ihya.

figures.name: Sana'i of Ghazna
figures.evidence: Treats direct knowledge of God through mystical unveiling in Hadiqat al-Haqiqa.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy attains direct intuitive knowledge of God through rational-mystical progression.

figures.name: Ruzbihan Baqli
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct gnostic knowledge in interpreting ecstatic states of great mystics.

figures.name: Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi
figures.evidence: Transmitted earlier Sufi teachings on direct knowledge of God through his order.

figures.name: Baha ud-Din Walad
figures.evidence: Ma'arif centers on direct experiential knowledge of God beyond rational theology.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Integrates direct knowledge by presence (huḍūrī) with philosophical illumination theory.

figures.name: Ibn Mashish
figures.evidence: His prayer emphasizes direct gnosis of divine reality beyond rational knowledge.

figures.name: Auhad al-Din Kirmani
figures.evidence: Developed gnosis themes from Ibn Arabi in Persian mystical poetry.

figures.name: Ibn Arabi
figures.evidence: Distinguished gnosis from discursive knowledge throughout mystical writings.

figures.name: Najm al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Treats direct knowledge of God as goal in The Path of God's Bondsmen.

figures.name: Umar Ibn al-Farid
figures.evidence: Poetry conveys direct experiential knowledge of God characteristic of Sufi gnosis.

figures.name: Shams-i-Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct experiential knowledge over bookish learning in transforming Rumi's spiritual path.

figures.name: Abu'l-Hasan al-Shadhili
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct experiential knowledge of God in Shadhili method.

figures.name: Jalal ad-Din Rumi
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct experiential knowledge of God throughout Fihi Ma Fihi discourses.

figures.name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
figures.evidence: Systematized gnosis as knowledge of divine names' manifestation in I'jaz al-Bayan.

figures.name: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi
figures.evidence: Poetic works emphasize direct experiential gnosis beyond discursive knowledge.

figures.name: Ibn Sab'in
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct gnosis in Budd al-'arif as path to absolute unity.

figures.name: Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi
figures.evidence: Passed on Shadhili gnosis teachings to third generation of the order.

figures.name: Ibn Ata Allah al-Iskandari
figures.evidence: Hikam extensively treats direct knowledge of God beyond rational discourse.

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri
figures.evidence: Discussed gnosis as realization of unity in his metaphysical writings.

figures.name: Sharaf al-Din Maneri
figures.evidence: Discusses direct experiential knowledge of God in his spiritual correspondence.

figures.name: Mahmud Shabistari
figures.evidence: Gulshan-i Raz distinguishes direct gnosis from rational knowledge throughout.

figures.name: Hafez
figures.evidence: Repeatedly invokes direct mystical knowledge in the Divan's ghazals.

figures.name: Shah Ni'matullah Wali
figures.evidence: Taught direct gnosis as path's culmination in his spiritual instruction.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: United philosophical epistemology with Sufi gnosis in his mystical philosophy.

figures.name: Ali Shir Nava'i
figures.evidence: Khamsa conveys Sufi gnosis themes within Persianate literary tradition through Chagatai.

figures.name: Shaykh Zarruq
figures.evidence: Integrated gnosis with jurisprudence in his reform of Shadhili method.

figures.name: 'A'isha al-Ba'uniyya
figures.evidence: Articulated experiential knowledge of God in her mystical treatises.

figures.name: Aisha al-Ba'uniyya
figures.evidence: Discusses direct experiential knowledge of God in her mystical compositions.

figures.name: Abd al-Wahhab al-Sha'rani
figures.evidence: Treats gnosis as goal of Sufi path in works on spiritual realization.

figures.name: Fuzuli
figures.evidence: Treats mystical gnosis in Hadikat al-suada exploring Karbala's spiritual significance.

figures.name: Hamza Fansuri
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct gnosis of God in his mystical poetry tradition.

figures.name: Mir Fendereski
figures.evidence: Combined philosophical demonstration with mystical gnosis in his teachings.

figures.name: Mulla Sadra
figures.evidence: Unites gnosis with demonstration in The Elixir of the Gnostics.

figures.name: Mulla Muhsin Fayd Kashani
figures.evidence: Merged philosophical and mystical gnosis in works bridging Sadra and Sufism.

figures.name: Mohsen Fayz Kashani
figures.evidence: Integrated mystical gnosis with Sadrian philosophy in his synthesis.

figures.name: Abd al-Rauf al-Singkili
figures.evidence: Taught gnostic knowledge as culmination of Sufi path in his Malay writings.

figures.name: Dara Shikoh
figures.evidence: Sirr-i-Akbar explores direct experiential knowledge of God through comparative mysticism.

figures.name: Muhammad Yusuf al-Maqassari
figures.evidence: Emphasized direct spiritual knowledge in his Sufi pedagogy.

figures.name: Sultan Bahu
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct gnosis through the single letter Alef in his poetry and prose.

figures.name: Bedil Dehlawi
figures.evidence: Elaborates direct mystical knowledge in philosophical-poetic idiom unique to Sabk-i Hindi.

figures.name: Ismail Hakki Bursevi
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct gnosis of God as goal in his mystical teachings.

figures.name: Ibrahim Haqqi Erzurumi
figures.evidence: Marifetname structures spiritual knowledge through both rational and mystical paths.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Arabi al-Darqawi
figures.evidence: Taught direct gnosis of God as the goal of the Shadhili path.

figures.name: Abd al-Qadir al-Jaza'iri
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct mystical knowledge in his spiritual teachings and writings.

figures.name: Khawaja Ghulam Farid
figures.evidence: Conveyed gnosis themes in his mystical poetry within Chishti-Sabiri framework.

figures.name: Ahmad al-Alawi
figures.evidence: Taught direct experiential knowledge of divine realities through spiritual unveiling.

figures.name: Rene Guenon
figures.evidence: Insights into Christian Esoterism distinguishes direct gnosis from exoteric theological knowledge.

figures.name: Qalandar Baba Auliya
figures.evidence: Writings emphasize direct experiential knowledge of God through Chishti contemplative methods.

figures.name: Hashim Larijani
figures.evidence: As mystic scholar, would have treated direct knowledge of God in teachings.

figures.name: Mirza Mahdi Elahi Qomshehei
figures.evidence: As philosopher-poet, may have bridged philosophical and mystical knowledge traditions.

figures.name: Muhammad Husayn Tabatabaei
figures.evidence: Integrated mystical gnosis with philosophy in his writings on Islamic spirituality.

figures.name: Frithjof Schuon
figures.evidence: Emphasizes direct gnosis as core to spiritual realization in his Shadhili teachings.

figures.name: Martin Lings
figures.evidence: Shadhili orientation emphasizes direct mystical knowledge in his hagiographic work.

figures.name: Mohammad-Taqi Ja'fari
figures.evidence: Combined philosophical epistemology with mystical gnosis in comprehensive Islamic thought.

figures.name: Khwaja Shamsuddin Azeemi
figures.evidence: Azeemia order emphasizes direct experiential knowledge of divine realities through muraqaba.

figures.name: Yousef Madani Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Grand ayatollah with mystical orientation would have engaged gnosis within Shia spirituality.

figures.name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
figures.evidence: Integrates gnosis with sacred knowledge in Knowledge and the Sacred.

figures.name: Nasrollah Pourjavady
figures.evidence: His work on mysticism necessarily engages gnosis as central Sufi concept.

figures.name: Seyed Ali Asghar Dastgheib
figures.evidence: Direct knowledge of God central to mystical teaching in Iranian Shia context.

figures.name: Ali Asghar Mosleh
figures.evidence: Worked on integrating mystical epistemology with philosophical methodology.

concepts.definition_ar: المعرفة الذوقية المباشرة لله فوق الاستدلال العقلي
concepts.definition_ur: اللہ کی براہ راست ذوقی معرفت جو عقلی استدلال سے بالاتر ہے

concepts.name: Ilm al-Hay'a (mathematical cosmography)
concepts.definition: The science of the heavenly spheres, combining observation with geometric modeling.

figures.name: Al-Khwarizmi
figures.evidence: Compiled astronomical tables adapting Indian and Greek models for Baghdad's latitude.

figures.name: Ma'mun al-Rashid
figures.evidence: Commissioned astronomical observations and Ptolemaic works translated at Baghdad observatory.

figures.name: Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi
figures.evidence: Major works on celestial spheres including Kitab al-Madkhal al-Kabir ila Ilm Ahkam al-Nujum.

figures.name: Al-Farghani
figures.evidence: Kitab fi Jawami Ilm al-Nujum systematized Ptolemaic cosmography for Arabic audiences.

figures.name: Banu Musa
figures.evidence: Conducted astronomical observations and contributed to planetary theory refinements.

figures.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
figures.evidence: Advanced Ptolemaic astronomy through original works on planetary theory and observational refinements.

figures.name: Al-Battani
figures.evidence: Opus astronomicum systematized spherical astronomy with refined trigonometric methods.

figures.name: Al-Sufi
figures.evidence: Book of Fixed Stars systematically mapped celestial sphere with updated stellar positions.

figures.name: Ibn al-Haytham
figures.evidence: Doubts Concerning Ptolemy systematically challenged Ptolemaic astronomical models.

figures.name: Al-Biruni
figures.evidence: Al-Qānūn al-Mas'ūdī systematizes astronomical models and spherical geometry.

figures.name: Al-Zarqali
figures.evidence: Advanced planetary theory and produced the Toledan Tables refining celestial models.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.evidence: Reformed astronomical models in treatises, created Solar Hijri calendar based on precise observations.

figures.name: al-Jazari
figures.evidence: Water clocks in his work require astronomical knowledge for timekeeping mechanisms.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Developed planetary models with Tusi-couple device described in Zij-i Ilkhani.

figures.name: Zakariya al-Qazwini
figures.evidence: Aja'ib al-Makhluqat systematically describes celestial spheres and astronomical phenomena.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Authored Nihayat al-Idrak on Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's cosmography system.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Jami' al-Mabadi' wa'l-Ghayat treats planetary theory and spherical astronomy systematically.

figures.name: Kamal al-Din al-Farisi
figures.evidence: Studied under Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī, transmitting Ṭūsī's astronomical models.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah discusses astronomical sciences as part of civilizational knowledge.

figures.name: Al-Kashi
figures.evidence: Sullam al-sama' is a major work on mathematical cosmography and planetary theory.

figures.name: Ulugh Beg
figures.evidence: Built Samarkand Observatory and systematized spherical astronomy in Zij-i Sultani.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Authored Zij-i Sultani, refining mathematical cosmography at Samarkand observatory.

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.evidence: Patronized astronomers and established observatory under Ali Qushji in Istanbul.

figures.name: Piri Reis
figures.evidence: Kitab-ı Bahriye applies celestial navigation using spherical cosmography for maritime routes.

figures.name: Taqi al-Din
figures.evidence: Built Istanbul Observatory and produced astronomical observations advancing celestial sphere models.

figures.name: Shaykh Bahai
figures.evidence: Known for astronomical work in Safavid Isfahan as polymath and Shaykh al-Islam.

figures.name: Katip Celebi
figures.evidence: Cataloged astronomical works in Kashf al-Zunun including treatises on cosmography.

figures.name: Ibrahim Haqqi Erzurumi
figures.evidence: Marifetname Book 1 blends Ptolemaic cosmography with Islamic theological cosmology.

figures.name: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi
figures.evidence: Authored Rasāʼil al-Kalanbawī fī ʻilm al-falak on astronomical sciences.

figures.name: Abbasgulu Bakikhanov
figures.evidence: Asrar al-Malakut (Secrets of the Heavenly Realm) suggests cosmological interests.

figures.name: Abdus Salam
figures.evidence: Advanced theoretical physics of fundamental forces and particle cosmology.

concepts.definition_ar: علم الأفلاك الجامع بين الرصد والنمذجة الهندسية
concepts.definition_ur: افلاکیات کا علم جو مشاہدے اور ہندسی نمونوں کو جوڑتا ہے

concepts.name: Tashrih (anatomy)
concepts.definition: The study of the body's structure, where Arabic-writing physicians extended and corrected Galen.

figures.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
figures.evidence: Book of the Ten Treatises of the Eye advanced detailed anatomical description of ocular structures.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated anatomical works from Greek medical tradition.

figures.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
figures.evidence: Advanced anatomical knowledge in 'Kitab al-Hawi' through dissection and clinical practice.

figures.name: Al-Zahrawi
figures.evidence: Al-Tasrif systematically describes surgical anatomy and procedures with detailed illustrations.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Advanced anatomical understanding in medical encyclopedia Miftah al-Tibb.

figures.name: Ibn Zuhr
figures.evidence: Advanced anatomical description and surgical technique in al-Taysir, correcting Galenic errors.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nafis
figures.evidence: Discovered pulmonary circulation in his Commentary on Anatomy in Avicenna's Canon.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: As physician, transmitted anatomical knowledge in medical writings.

concepts.definition_ar: دراسة بنية الجسم حيث طوّر الأطباء العرب علم جالينوس وصحّحوه
concepts.definition_ur: جسم کی ساخت کا مطالعہ جس میں عرب اطباء نے جالینوس کو آگے بڑھایا

concepts.name: Kimiya (alchemy)
concepts.definition: The tradition of transforming substances, searching for the elixir, and laboratory technique.

figures.name: Ja'far al-Sadiq
figures.evidence: Transmitted alchemical knowledge to his student Jabir ibn Hayyan according to tradition.

figures.name: Jabir ibn Hayyan
figures.evidence: Authored foundational alchemical corpus including Kitab al-Khawass and Book of the Composition of Alchemy.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: Wrote on alchemical theory integrating it with Aristotelian natural philosophy.

figures.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
figures.evidence: Systematized chemical classification and laboratory methods in 'Kitab al-Asrar' (Secret of Secrets).

figures.name: Ibn al-Nadim
figures.evidence: Al-Fihrist contains extensive section on alchemists and their treatises.

concepts.definition_ar: تقليد تحويل المواد والبحث عن الإكسير والتقنية المخبرية
concepts.definition_ur: مادوں کی تبدیلی، اکسیر کی تلاش اور تجربہ گاہی تکنیک کی روایت

concepts.name: Al-Jabr (algebra)
concepts.definition: The systematic manipulation of unknowns as equations, from al-Khwarizmi onward.

figures.name: Al-Khwarizmi
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Jabr wa'l-Muqabala systematically established algebra as solving equations by restoration and balancing.

figures.name: Ma'mun al-Rashid
figures.evidence: Patronized al-Khwarizmi who dedicated his algebra treatise to Ma'mun.

figures.name: Banu Musa
figures.evidence: Translated Greek mathematical works including Apollonius's Conics into Arabic.

figures.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
figures.evidence: Contributed to number theory with amicable numbers and the Thabit number theorem.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.evidence: Extended al-Khwarizmi's algebra with geometric solutions to cubic equations in mathematical treatises.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Systematized algebraic methods in Talkhis a'mal al-hisab, foundational for Maghrebi tradition.

figures.name: Al-Kashi
figures.evidence: Miftah al-hisab systematically treats algebraic methods and equations.

figures.name: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi
figures.evidence: Mathematics master in 18th-century Ottoman curriculum would have taught algebra.

concepts.definition_ar: المعالجة المنهجية للمجهولات كمعادلات من الخوارزمي فصاعداً
concepts.definition_ur: خوارزمی سے شروع ہونے والا مجہولات کو مساوات کے طور پر حل کرنے کا منظم طریقہ

concepts.name: Ilm al-Manazir (optics)
concepts.definition: The geometrical and experimental science of vision and light.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: Works on optics develop geometric theories of vision and light.

figures.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
figures.evidence: Translated Greek optical texts that laid groundwork for later Arabic optical sciences.

figures.name: Ibn al-Haytham
figures.evidence: Book of Optics revolutionized understanding of vision through systematic experimentation.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Explained the rainbow through refraction in Tanqih al-Manazir.

figures.name: Kamal al-Din al-Farisi
figures.evidence: Tanqīḥ al-Manāẓir systematizes Ibn al-Haytham's optics with experimental refinements.

concepts.definition_ar: العلم الهندسي والتجريبي للبصر والضوء
concepts.definition_ur: بصر اور روشنی کا ہندسی اور تجرباتی علم

concepts.name: Akhlat (humoral theory)
concepts.definition: Galenic doctrine of four bodily humors whose balance defines health.

figures.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
figures.evidence: Translated Galen's works on humoral theory from Greek to Arabic for the House of Wisdom.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated Galenic medical works on humoral theory into Arabic.

figures.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
figures.evidence: Refined humoral theory in 'Kitab al-Mansuri' with clinical observations and balancing regimens.

figures.name: Al-Zahrawi
figures.evidence: Al-Tasrif applies Galenic humoral theory in medical treatments and diagnosis.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Applied Galenic humoral theory systematically in his medical writings.

figures.name: Ibn Zuhr
figures.evidence: Applied humoral theory clinically in al-Taysir with detailed diagnostic and therapeutic protocols.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nafis
figures.evidence: Applied humoral theory in his medical works as physician following Galenic tradition.

concepts.definition_ar: نظرية جالينوس في الأخلاط الأربعة التي يحدد توازنها الصحة
concepts.definition_ur: جالینوس کا نظریہ چار مزاجوں کا جن کے توازن سے صحت متعین ہوتی ہے

concepts.name: Adwa (contagion debate)
concepts.definition: Whether diseases transmit person to person, debated against a prophetic saying denying contagion.

figures.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
figures.evidence: Argued for disease transmission in writings on infectious diseases, contra dominant views.

concepts.definition_ar: هل تنتقل الأمراض بين الأشخاص في ضوء حديث نبوي ينفي العدوى
concepts.definition_ur: کیا بیماریاں لوگوں میں منتقل ہوتی ہیں حدیث نبوی کی روشنی میں

concepts.name: Hisab (arithmetic and reckoning)
concepts.definition: Calculation for commerce, inheritance, astronomy, and timekeeping.

figures.name: Al-Khwarizmi
figures.evidence: Introduced Hindu-Arabic decimal system and algorithms for arithmetic calculation to Islamic world.

figures.name: Al-Farghani
figures.evidence: Performed astronomical calculations for planetary positions and calendar systems.

figures.name: Banu Musa
figures.evidence: Advanced computational techniques for solving geometric and astronomical problems.

figures.name: Al-Battani
figures.evidence: Refined trigonometric calculations for astronomy in De motu stellarum.

figures.name: Al-Biruni
figures.evidence: Al-Tafhim treats arithmetic, reckoning methods, and calendrical calculations.

figures.name: Al-Zarqali
figures.evidence: Developed computational methods for astronomical calculations and calendar reckoning.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Authored Talkhis on computational methods for inheritance, commerce, and practical calculation.

figures.name: Al-Kashi
figures.evidence: The Calculators' Key treats arithmetic comprehensively for practical and scientific calculation.

figures.name: Ulugh Beg
figures.evidence: Advanced trigonometric calculations for astronomical purposes in Zij-i Sultani.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Developed computational methods for astronomical tables and calculations.

figures.name: Shaykh Bahai
figures.evidence: The Essentials of Arithmetic advances arithmetic methods for practical and astronomical use.

concepts.definition_ar: الحساب للتجارة والمواريث والفلك والتوقيت
concepts.definition_ur: تجارت، وراثت، فلکیات اور وقت کے لیے حساب

concepts.name: Tajriba (experiment and tested experience)
concepts.definition: Deliberately controlled trial as a source of knowledge in medicine and optics.

figures.name: Jabir ibn Hayyan
figures.evidence: Systematized experimental methodology in alchemy, emphasizing controlled observation and replication.

figures.name: Al-Razi (Rhazes)
figures.evidence: First controlled clinical trials documented in 'al-Judari wa al-Hasbah' distinguishing smallpox.

figures.name: Miskawayh
figures.evidence: Tajārib al-Umam title itself emphasizes historical experience as knowledge source.

figures.name: Al-Zahrawi
figures.evidence: Al-Tasrif documents surgical instruments and techniques tested through clinical practice.

figures.name: Ibn al-Haytham
figures.evidence: Book of Optics pioneered experimental method with controlled trials using camera obscura.

figures.name: Al-Biruni
figures.evidence: Advocated empirical observation in Kitab al-Hind and astronomical investigations.

figures.name: Ibn Zuhr
figures.evidence: Emphasized clinical observation and empirical testing over theoretical speculation in al-Taysir.

figures.name: Kamal al-Din al-Farisi
figures.evidence: Used glass spheres filled with water to experimentally demonstrate rainbow formation.

figures.name: Taqi al-Din
figures.evidence: Conducted systematic observations at Istanbul Observatory to test astronomical theories.

concepts.definition_ar: الاختبار المضبوط المقصود مصدراً للمعرفة في الطب والبصريات
concepts.definition_ur: طب اور بصریات میں معرفت کے ماخذ کے طور پر جان بوجھ کر کیا گیا منضبط تجربہ

concepts.name: Handasa (geometry)
concepts.definition: Euclidean geometry extended by Arabic-writing mathematicians, feeding astronomy and optics.

figures.name: Al-Khwarizmi
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry to practical cartography and measurement in geographical works.

figures.name: Ma'mun al-Rashid
figures.evidence: Funded translation of Euclid's Elements and patronized geometric research.

figures.name: Al-Farghani
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry extensively in measuring celestial spheres and distances.

figures.name: Banu Musa
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Hiyal contains advanced geometric constructions for mechanical devices and automata.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated Euclidean and other Greek geometric texts into Arabic.

figures.name: Thabit ibn Qurra
figures.evidence: Extended Euclidean geometry in Liber de figura sectore on the transversal theorem.

figures.name: Al-Battani
figures.evidence: Applied spherical geometry to astronomy, improving Ptolemaic models in Opus astronomicum.

figures.name: Al-Sufi
figures.evidence: Applied geometric methods to map stellar coordinates and constellations systematically.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nadim
figures.evidence: Al-Fihrist documents geometers and translations of Euclid and Apollonius.

figures.name: Ibn al-Haytham
figures.evidence: Applied advanced geometry to solve optical problems in Book of Optics.

figures.name: Al-Biruni
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry extensively in astronomical and geodetic works.

figures.name: Al-Zarqali
figures.evidence: Applied geometry to design the improved astrolabe (Saphea) and other instruments.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry to solve cubic equations and astronomical problems in his works.

figures.name: al-Jazari
figures.evidence: Kitab fi Ma'rifat al-Hiyal al-Handasiya systematically applies geometric principles to mechanical devices.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Edited Euclid's Elements in Tahrir Usul al-Uqlidis for Islamic curriculum.

figures.name: Zakariya al-Qazwini
figures.evidence: Athar al-Bilad includes geographic descriptions relying on geometric calculations.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry in astronomical works under Tusi's influence.

figures.name: Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi
figures.evidence: Transmitted Euclidean geometry in curriculum, integrating it with astronomical applications.

figures.name: Kamal al-Din al-Farisi
figures.evidence: Applied geometric ray tracing to analyze refraction through spherical droplets.

figures.name: Al-Kashi
figures.evidence: Risala al-muhitiyya computes pi to 16 decimals using geometric methods.

figures.name: Ulugh Beg
figures.evidence: Applied Euclidean geometry to astronomical calculations in his observatory work.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Applied advanced geometry to astronomical modeling in observatory work.

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.evidence: Patronized mathematical sciences for artillery, architecture, and urban planning in Constantinople.

figures.name: Piri Reis
figures.evidence: Piri Reis map demonstrates geometric projection techniques for world cartography.

figures.name: Taqi al-Din
figures.evidence: Applied geometric methods to astronomical instruments and mechanical device design.

figures.name: Shaykh Bahai
figures.evidence: Applied geometry in architectural projects including Isfahan's Maidan complex design.

figures.name: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi
figures.evidence: As Ottoman master of mathematics, systematically taught Euclidean geometry.

concepts.definition_ar: الهندسة الإقليدية التي طوّرها الرياضيون العرب لخدمة الفلك والبصريات
concepts.definition_ur: اقلیدسی ہندسہ جسے عرب ریاضی دانوں نے فلکیات اور بصریات کے لیے ترقی دی

concepts.name: Imama (Shia imamate)
concepts.definition: Shia doctrine that leadership of the community belongs to designated infallible Imams.

figures.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
figures.evidence: Central figure in Shia doctrine of divinely-designated leadership through Prophet's family.

figures.name: Hasan ibn Ali
figures.evidence: As second Shia Imam, embodied the doctrine of divinely-guided leadership after Ali.

figures.name: Husayn ibn Ali
figures.evidence: His refusal of Yazid's bay'a grounded Shia doctrine of divinely-designated leadership.

figures.name: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya
figures.evidence: Claimed by some Kaysaniyya groups as rightful Imam after Hasan and Husayn's deaths.

figures.name: Ali ibn al-Husayn
figures.evidence: His Risalat al-Huquq articulates rights including those of the Imam as divinely guided leader.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Baqir
figures.evidence: As 5th Imam, developed early Shia doctrine of designated infallible leadership through teaching.

figures.name: Zayd ibn Ali
figures.evidence: Founded Zaydi imamate doctrine requiring armed uprising and scholarly qualifications for Imams.

figures.name: Ja'far al-Sadiq
figures.evidence: Elaborated theory of Imamate and esoteric knowledge transmission in his Baghdad teachings.

figures.name: Ali al-Ridha
figures.evidence: As Eighth Imam, transmitted Shia doctrine of divinely designated leadership through Imams.

figures.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
figures.evidence: Defended Ismaili imamate doctrine in polemics against rival claims.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Jawad
figures.evidence: Held office of Imam after Ali al-Ridha, continuing Shia conception of divinely guided leadership.

figures.name: Al-Kulayni
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Kafi's entire structure organized around transmitting teachings of the Imams.

figures.name: Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi
figures.evidence: Established Fatimid Caliphate claiming descent from Ali and Ismaili imamate doctrine.

figures.name: Al-Masudi
figures.evidence: Documents Shia doctrines of the Imamate in his historical accounts.

figures.name: Ibn Babawayh
figures.evidence: Comprehensive treatment of Imamate doctrine in Eʿteqādāt al-Emāmīya and Uyun Akhbar Al-Ridha.

figures.name: Al-Mufid
figures.evidence: Systematized Twelver Imamah doctrine in Kitab al-Irshad on the Twelve Imams.

figures.name: Sharif al-Radi
figures.evidence: Compiled Nahj al-Balagha, key anthology of Imam Ali's sermons on leadership.

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Detailed theory of imamate and leadership in Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyyah.

figures.name: Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din al-Shirazi
figures.evidence: Major Isma'ili theologian defending imamate doctrine in Diwan and other works.

figures.name: Nasir Khusraw
figures.evidence: Defends Fatimid Ismaili imamate doctrine as Hujjat-i Khorasan in theological treatises.

figures.name: Arwa al-Sulayhi
figures.evidence: Ruled as Sulayhid queen implementing Tayyibi Ismaili imamate doctrine for 70 years.

figures.name: Hasan-i Sabbah
figures.evidence: Established Nizari Ismaili state at Alamut with doctrine of designated Imam's authority.

figures.name: Al-Shahrastani
figures.evidence: Extensively documents Shia imamate doctrines across sects in Milal wa-al-nihal.

figures.name: Al-Bahrani
figures.evidence: Bahraini context and theological classification suggests transmission of Shia imamate doctrine.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Systematized Twelver Shia imamate doctrine in Minhaj al-karamah against Sunni critics.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: Philosophically grounded Shia imamate doctrine in his theological synthesis.

figures.name: Shah Ismail I
figures.evidence: Established Twelver Shiism as state doctrine, enforcing Imami belief throughout Iran.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Defended Twelver imamate doctrine as leading Shia theologian-philosopher in Safavid court.

figures.name: Shah Abbas I
figures.evidence: Established Isfahan as Twelver Shia capital, enforcing Imami doctrine as state religion.

figures.name: Ayatollah Khomeini
figures.evidence: Defended Shia imamate doctrine extensively in 'Kashf al-Asrar' and other works.

figures.name: Muhammad Husayn Tabatabaei
figures.evidence: Systematically expounded Shia imamate doctrine in Shi'ite Islam.

figures.name: Ahmad Azari Qomi
figures.evidence: Core Shi'a doctrine transmitted by all Shi'a clerics; fundamental to his religious authority in Qom.

figures.name: Ali Shariati
figures.evidence: Redefined Shia Imamate as revolutionary leadership model in Red Shi'ism vs. Black Shi'ism.

figures.name: Abbas-Ali Soleimani
figures.evidence: As Iranian Shia cleric, would have transmitted core doctrine of infallible Imams' authority.

figures.name: Hassan Khomeini
figures.evidence: As Shia cleric in Qom, teaches foundational Twelver Shia theology of Imamate.

figures.name: Muqtada al-Sadr
figures.evidence: Named Mahdi Army after hidden Twelfth Imam, affirming Shia imamate doctrine.

figures.name: Yasser Al-Habib
figures.evidence: Upholds traditional Twelver Shia doctrine of divinely-appointed Imamate in public discourse.

concepts.definition_ar: عقيدة الشيعة بأن قيادة الأمة حق أئمة معصومين معيّنين بالنص
concepts.definition_ur: شیعہ عقیدہ کہ امت کی قیادت معصوم ائمہ کا حق ہے جو نص سے مقرر ہیں

concepts.name: Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur (exegesis by transmitted reports)
concepts.definition: Explaining the Qur'an mainly through prophetic reports and early authorities.

figures.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
figures.evidence: Mushaf Ali attributed as early Quranic commentary drawing on prophetic teachings.

figures.name: Al-Aswad ibn Yazid
figures.evidence: Transmitted Qur'anic interpretations from Ibn Mas'ud and Aisha to Kufan tradition.

figures.name: Alqama ibn Qays
figures.evidence: Transmitted Ibn Mas'ud's Qur'anic interpretations to the Kufan school.

figures.name: Masruq ibn al-Ajda

figures.evidence: Authored al-Wafi, major hadith collection applying rijal criticism to Shia traditions.

figures.name: Katip Celebi
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Zunun systematically catalogs bio-bibliographical data on Islamic scholars and transmitters.

figures.name: Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlawi
figures.evidence: Known as Muhaddith al-Dihlawi for transmitting hadith sciences from Shah Waliullah.

figures.name: Sayyid Ahmad Khan
figures.evidence: Questioned traditional hadith methodology, accepting only mutawātir reports in some works.

figures.name: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi
figures.evidence: Taught hadith sciences at Deoband, establishing rigorous transmitted scholarship standards.

figures.name: Muhammad Shams-ul-Haq Azimabadi
figures.evidence: Specialized in hadith sciences, transmitting biographical evaluation methods of his era.

figures.name: Muhammad Talha Kandhlawi
figures.evidence: Specialized in hadith sciences at Kandhla, a major center of hadith transmission in Deobandi tradition.
